title: Mission Experience Week Gives Participants a Firsthand Look at Life in Ministry
excerpt: Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) recently concluded its Mission Experience Week, welcoming participants for several days of Bible study, evangelism, ministry training, and fellowship at YEF in…
paragraphs: Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) recently concluded its Mission Experience Week, welcoming participants for several days of Bible study, evangelism, ministry training, and fellowship at YEF in Florida. Designed to provide a firsthand look at life in Christian ministry, the program gave participants the opportunity to learn, serve, and grow alongside YEF leaders while experiencing the daily rhythm of evangelism and discipleship.

The week began with an introduction to YEF's mission and vision, followed by a campus tour and orientation. Participants became acquainted with one another through fellowship and icebreaker activities before joining ministry seminars that explored the biblical foundations of evangelism, discipleship, and Christian leadership. Throughout the week, they studied God's Word together, participated in discussions, and reflected on how they could apply biblical principles in their own lives and future ministry.

A central part of the experience was daily campus evangelism. Participants joined YEF members in visiting local universities, including the University of Central Florida and Seminole State College, where they shared the Gospel with students and invited them to study the Bible. Although some campuses were quieter because of the summer semester and final examinations, participants faithfully engaged in conversations with students and witnessed firsthand the importance of perseverance in evangelism regardless of the circumstances.

Alongside outreach, participants attended regular Bible studies that demonstrated YEF's discipleship ministry. Through studies in Scripture, they observed how God's Word is taught, discussed, and applied in helping young people grow in their faith. These sessions also provided opportunities to ask questions, deepen their understanding of the Gospel, and witness the importance of building lasting relationships through ongoing discipleship.

Throughout the program, participants also received practical ministry training in areas such as leadership, teamwork, communication, and serving within the local church. By observing and participating in daily ministry activities, they gained valuable insight into the commitment, preparation, and heart required to faithfully serve Christ.

Mission Experience Week also included times of fellowship and recreation that strengthened relationships among participants and ministry leaders. Shared meals, conversations, and group activities created an atmosphere where friendships quickly developed, allowing participants to encourage one another while growing together in faith.

As the week drew to a close, participants gathered for YEF's Friday Prayer meeting, joining the fellowship in seeking God's guidance and giving thanks for all that He had accomplished throughout the week. The prayer service served as a meaningful conclusion to the program, reminding everyone that every aspect of ministry begins and continues through dependence on God.

Following the prayer meeting, participants enjoyed time together at Disney Springs, where they relaxed, shared meals, and reflected on the experiences they had shared throughout the week. The group also spent time exercising together at the gym, emphasizing the importance of caring for both body and spirit while continuing to build friendships in a relaxed setting.

During their final days in Florida, participants took time to reflect on the many lessons they had received through Bible study, evangelism, seminars, prayer, and fellowship. Many expressed gratitude for the opportunity to experience ministry firsthand and to witness the joy and challenges of faithfully serving the Lord alongside YEF leaders.

Mission Experience Week reflects YEF's ongoing commitment to raising the next generation of Christian leaders by providing opportunities for young people to experience biblical discipleship in action. Through studying God's Word, participating in evangelism, serving alongside experienced ministers, and building Christ-centered relationships, participants left encouraged to continue growing in their faith and sharing the Gospel in their own communities.

YEF looks forward to welcoming future participants as the ministry continues equipping young people around the world to become faithful disciples of Christ and leaders who will carry the Gospel to the next generation.

title: YEF Ethiopia Continues Summer Training Through Bible Study and Evangelism
excerpt: Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) Ethiopia continues its summer training program as members dedicate themselves to both biblical instruction and practical ministry. The program is designed to…
paragraphs: Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) Ethiopia continues its summer training program as members dedicate themselves to both biblical instruction and practical ministry. The program is designed to strengthen future leaders through a balance of studying God's Word, developing ministry skills, and participating in evangelism.

Each morning begins with Bible study centered on the New Testament Epistles, with a particular emphasis on the themes of salvation, faith, and spiritual growth. Brother Samuel Mitiku is currently reviewing the Book of Romans while continuing his study of Galatians, building a deeper understanding of the Gospel and the biblical foundations of the Christian life.

Alongside Scripture study, the training includes practical instruction in ministry skills such as teaching the Bible, writing ministry articles, and communicating the Gospel clearly and effectively. After each session, Brother Samuel records personal reflections on what he has learned, helping reinforce biblical truths while developing the ability to share them with others.

During the afternoons, the team continues its outreach through onsite evangelism in Addis Ababa. Recent outreach efforts have taken place at Addis Ababa University and the Abrehot Public Library, where members sought opportunities to meet students and young adults and invite them to study the Bible. Although the university's academic break resulted in fewer students on campus, and periods of heavy rainfall limited outreach activities, the team remained faithful in sharing the Gospel with those they encountered.

Looking ahead, YEF Ethiopia plans to expand its outreach by visiting additional locations where larger numbers of university students and young people gather. The fellowship remains committed to creating opportunities for meaningful conversations, Bible studies, and continued discipleship.

Through this summer training program, YEF Ethiopia is investing in the next generation of Christian leaders by equipping them with a solid biblical foundation and practical ministry experience. The fellowship asks for continued prayer for Brother Samuel's spiritual growth and training, as well as for open doors to share the Gospel with many young people throughout Ethiopia.

YEF Ethiopia looks forward to seeing God continue His work through faithful discipleship, evangelism, and the raising of leaders who will serve Christ and proclaim the Gospel throughout their communities.

title: YEF Africa Strengthens Members Through Bible Training on Salvation, Grace, and Faith in Christ
excerpt: Youth Evangelical Fellowship Africa recently continued its ongoing Bible training program, bringing together members from several African nations for a time of fellowship, learning, and spiritual…
paragraphs: Youth Evangelical Fellowship Africa recently continued its ongoing Bible training program, bringing together members from several African nations for a time of fellowship, learning, and spiritual encouragement through the study of Scripture.

The training focused on the Christian message of salvation and the relationship between faith, grace, and new life in Christ. Through the study, participants reflected on humanity’s need for God’s grace and the hope offered through the life, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ. Discussions explored biblical teachings on forgiveness, redemption, and the assurance believers can find through faith.

Throughout the training, participants examined passages from the New Testament that emphasize God’s love and mercy toward humanity. The studies highlighted that salvation is a gift of grace and encouraged members to place their trust in God rather than relying solely on their own efforts or achievements. Participants were reminded of the transformative power of faith and the importance of living with gratitude, humility, and confidence in God’s promises.

The gathering also provided an opportunity for members to share reflections, testimonies, and personal insights from their studies. Through fellowship and discussion, participants encouraged one another and strengthened their commitment to continuing their spiritual growth and service within their local communities.

One participant reflected that the training served as a powerful reminder that true spiritual renewal comes through God’s grace and that faith provides both hope and direction in daily life. The discussion encouraged members to continue trusting God’s guidance while sharing the message of hope with others.

YEF Africa gives thanks for the opportunity to gather together across national boundaries for Bible training and fellowship. The ministry continues praying that participants will grow in faith, deepen their understanding of Scripture, and be equipped to serve students, communities, and future generations with wisdom, compassion, and a strong foundation in God’s Word.

title: YEF Orlando Combines Leadership Training, Bible Study, and Campus Outreach to Strengthen Student Ministry
excerpt: On May 26, 2026, YEF Orlando gathered for a leadership and teacher development session focused on prayer and spiritual dependence in ministry. Participants spent time reflecting on the importance of…
paragraphs: On May 26, 2026, YEF Orlando gathered for a leadership and teacher development session focused on prayer and spiritual dependence in ministry. Participants spent time reflecting on the importance of maintaining a strong prayer life and learning to rely on God’s guidance rather than personal strength while serving others. The training emphasized that effective ministry is rooted not only in knowledge and preparation, but also in faith, prayer, and dependence on the work of the Holy Spirit.

The gathering also provided an opportunity for participants to continue developing practical teaching skills and deepen their understanding of discipleship and spiritual leadership. Through ongoing training, YEF hopes to equip future leaders and Bible teachers who can serve students with wisdom, humility, and a strong foundation in Scripture.

Following the training, the group held a campus Bible study with students centered on Romans 1. The discussion focused on the existence of God and humanity’s response to the evidence of God revealed through creation. Participants reflected on how the natural world points to God's power and character, while also considering the importance of gratitude, faith, and seeking a deeper relationship with God.

The fellowship hopes that students will continue engaging thoughtfully with Scripture and grow in their understanding of faith through regular Bible study and discussion. In support of this goal, YEF Orlando has also been continuing to improve educational resources and teaching materials, including the development of updated study guides and presentation materials to help make Bible studies more engaging and accessible.

After the Bible study, members continued campus outreach by meeting students, inviting them to future Bible studies, and sharing information about upcoming fellowship activities both on and off campus. Through these efforts, the team hopes to create opportunities for meaningful conversations, spiritual growth, and Christian community among university students.

YEF Orlando continues praying for students, volunteers, and ministry leaders involved in campus outreach. The fellowship also prays that hearts may remain open to God’s Word and that the ministry may continue serving students with wisdom, compassion, and renewed purpose throughout the year.

title: “Filled With the Holy Spirit”: YEF Members Around the World Join Pentecost Retreats in Unity Worship Prayer and the Word of God
excerpt: During the Pentecost season, Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) members across multiple nations gathered together with local churches, ministries, and mission communities to reflect on the coming of…
paragraphs: During the Pentecost season, Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) members across multiple nations gathered together with local churches, ministries, and mission communities to reflect on the coming of the Holy Spirit, deepen their understanding of Scripture, and seek spiritual renewal through worship, prayer, fellowship, and Bible study. Across North America, Africa, Europe, Asia, and Oceania, believers united around the shared message of Pentecost and the continuing work of the Holy Spirit in the lives of Christians today.

In North America, YEF Orlando hosted a Pentecost Retreat at its headquarters in Florida, bringing together members and students for a weekend focused on worship, Bible study, prayer, and fellowship. Participants reflected on passages from Acts, John, and Romans that explored the promise of the Holy Spirit, the life of the early church, and the role of prayer and faith in the Christian life. Through discussions, worship, fellowship meals, and interactive activities, many participants shared that they experienced encouragement, spiritual renewal, and a deeper desire to depend on God in their daily lives.

Another Pentecost gathering in the United States focused on Jesus’ teaching in John 16 regarding the work of the Holy Spirit and Christ’s victory over the world. Participants reflected on the Holy Spirit as the One who guides believers into truth, strengthens faith, and helps Christians remain steadfast through challenges and uncertainty.

In Africa, believers gathered for Pentecost worship services and retreat programs centered on prayer, spiritual renewal, and the meaning of Pentecost. Messages focused on the Holy Spirit as Comforter, Teacher, and Guide while encouraging unity, faithful prayer, and continued spiritual growth. Participants were reminded of God’s presence and faithfulness as they continue serving in their communities and sharing the Gospel.

Across Europe, YEF members participated in Pentecost worship gatherings, Bible studies, and fellowship activities alongside local churches and students. Through teachings on the Holy Spirit, participants reflected on spiritual growth, personal renewal, and the importance of remaining faithful to God while continuing to serve others through evangelism, discipleship, and Christian fellowship.

In Asia, believers gathered for Pentecost services and special retreat programs focused on faith, discipleship, and the work of the Holy Spirit. In several locations, participants combined worship and Bible study with evangelism outreach and fellowship activities. Messages emphasized spiritual renewal, living by faith, and relying on God’s guidance while serving students and young adults within local communities.

Meanwhile, throughout Oceania and other mission fields, members joined worship services, prayer meetings, and Pentecost gatherings that encouraged believers to seek God more deeply and prepare for future ministry opportunities. Participants reflected on how the Holy Spirit continues to strengthen believers, guide the church, and empower Christians to live faithfully in the modern world.

One of the recurring themes throughout the various Pentecost gatherings was that Pentecost is not only a historical event recorded in Scripture, but also a continuing reminder of God's presence and work among His people. Through the gift of the Holy Spirit, believers are encouraged to grow in faith, deepen their relationship with God, strengthen Christian community, and continue sharing the hope of the Gospel with others.

As Pentecost celebrations concluded, many participants expressed gratitude for the opportunity to gather together in worship, study God's Word, and encourage one another in faith. YEF members around the world continue moving forward with renewed vision, praying that the lessons learned during Pentecost will inspire ongoing spiritual growth, stronger communities, and greater commitment to serving God and others throughout the year.

title: YEF Orlando Holds Pentecost Retreat Reflecting on the Holy Spirit, the Early Church, and the Mission of Believers
excerpt: From Saturday to Sunday, YEF Orlando and members from across Florida gathered together for a Pentecost Retreat centered on the Holy Spirit, prayer, discipleship, and the life of the early church.…
paragraphs: From Saturday to Sunday, YEF Orlando and members from across Florida gathered together for a Pentecost Retreat centered on the Holy Spirit, prayer, discipleship, and the life of the early church. Throughout the weekend, participants spent time in worship, Bible study, fellowship, reflection, and prayer while exploring the significance of Pentecost and its relevance for believers today.

The retreat opened with a study of Acts 2, reflecting on the coming of the Holy Spirit and the beginning of the Christian church. Throughout the day, participants continued with a series of Bible studies focusing on the promise of the Holy Spirit, God’s guidance in the lives of believers, and the role of prayer and faith in the Christian life. Additional studies explored the community life of the early church and how believers supported, encouraged, and worshiped together after Pentecost.

Between sessions, participants shared meals, fellowship, discussion, and group activities that helped strengthen relationships and build a greater sense of community. The day concluded with a time of guided prayer, personal reflection, and worship as attendees considered how they could apply the lessons of Pentecost in their daily lives.

Several students and guests also participated in the retreat, both in person and online. The fellowship was encouraged by their participation and continues praying that those who attended may continue growing in faith, developing a deeper understanding of Scripture, and experiencing the encouragement that comes through Christian community.

The second day of the retreat focused entirely on Pentecost and the work of the Holy Spirit. Through studies based on Acts 1 and 2, participants reflected on God’s promise to pour out His Spirit and the birth of the church as a community united in faith, worship, and mission. The message emphasized the role of the Holy Spirit in guiding, strengthening, and transforming believers, while reminding participants that God continues to work through His people today.

Participants also reflected on how Pentecost demonstrates God's desire to reach people from every background and nation. Through the Holy Spirit, believers are empowered to live with hope, serve others, grow in faith, and participate in the ongoing mission of sharing the Gospel with the world.

The retreat concluded with a time of prayer, fellowship, and reflection before participants enjoyed outdoor activities together. Many shared that the weekend provided encouragement, spiritual renewal, and a deeper appreciation for the work of the Holy Spirit in the life of the church.

YEF Orlando gives thanks for everyone who participated in the retreat and continues praying that the lessons learned through worship, prayer, Bible study, and fellowship will continue bearing fruit in the lives of those who attended. The fellowship also hopes that more students and young adults may have opportunities to experience spiritual growth, meaningful community, and a deeper understanding of God's love through future gatherings and ministry activities.

title: YEF Romania Reflects on Pentecost Through Worship Bible Study and Spiritual Renewal
excerpt: During the Pentecost weekend, YEF Romania participated in a local Pentecost Retreat, joining fellow believers for Bible studies, worship services, prayer, and fellowship. Throughout the retreat,…
paragraphs: During the Pentecost weekend, YEF Romania participated in a local Pentecost Retreat, joining fellow believers for Bible studies, worship services, prayer, and fellowship. Throughout the retreat, participants reflected on the work of the Holy Spirit, spiritual growth, and the importance of living faithfully as followers of Christ.

The retreat included several Bible studies that explored the role of the Holy Spirit in the life of believers, focusing on themes such as God’s presence, spiritual gifts, unity within the church, and the diversity of gifts and callings among believers. Participants were encouraged to understand more deeply how the Holy Spirit guides, strengthens, and equips Christians to serve God and one another.

The closing message focused on spiritual growth and the ongoing process of becoming more Christlike. Participants reflected on the importance of pursuing holiness, remaining faithful in daily life, and recognizing that the Christian journey involves continual dependence on God’s strength and guidance.

One regular Bible study student also participated in part of the retreat despite a demanding academic schedule. The fellowship was encouraged by the student’s commitment to spiritual growth and willingness to prioritize time in worship and Bible study while balancing university responsibilities.

Reflecting on the retreat, a YEF Romania member shared how one of the messages served as a powerful reminder of the importance of remaining spiritually alert and continuing to grow in faith. The retreat encouraged deeper reflection on personal transformation, prayer, and reliance upon the Holy Spirit rather than human strength. Participants were reminded that spiritual growth is an ongoing journey and that true change comes through God’s work within the heart.

The member also shared that the retreat renewed a desire to spend more time in prayer, engage more deeply with Scripture, and rely more fully on the Holy Spirit in both ministry and daily life. While serving through evangelism and Bible study, the retreat became a reminder that personal spiritual growth remains essential for every believer.

YEF Romania gives thanks for the opportunity to participate in the Pentecost Retreat and continues praying that the lessons learned through worship, Bible study, and fellowship will bear lasting fruit. The fellowship hopes that more students and young people throughout Romania may continue growing in faith, discovering God’s purpose for their lives, and experiencing spiritual renewal through the power of the Holy Spirit.

title: Joint Pentecost Retreat in Macau Encourages Spiritual Renewal Through Bible Study Evangelism and Fellowship
excerpt: From May 23–24, a Joint Pentecost Retreat was held at Macau Immanuel Church, bringing together ministers, missionaries, and members from several ministries and fellowships across Macau and China for…
paragraphs: From May 23–24, a Joint Pentecost Retreat was held at Macau Immanuel Church, bringing together ministers, missionaries, and members from several ministries and fellowships across Macau and China for a time of worship, Bible study, evangelism, prayer, and fellowship. Throughout the retreat, participants reflected on spiritual renewal, faith, and the continuing work of the Holy Spirit through the life of the church.

The first day of the retreat included three Bible teaching sessions, street evangelism outreach, and an evening of praise and prayer. During evangelism activities, participants also received new student contact information for future follow-up and Bible study invitation. Many attendees shared that the retreat became a meaningful source of encouragement, strength, and renewed passion for sharing the Gospel.

One of the Bible studies focused on Ezekiel 37 and reflected on the theme of revival through God’s Word and renewed hope, using the image of the valley of dry bones to encourage believers facing discouragement or spiritual exhaustion. Additional studies centered on the book of Romans, including reflections on faith, sin, salvation, and the meaning of living by faith in Christ. Through the messages and fellowship, participants shared that they were able to deepen their understanding of Scripture and grow spiritually throughout the retreat.

Members also testified that the outreach activities helped them become more confident and free in sharing the Gospel publicly in Macau. Although many people may initially appear uninterested in spiritual conversations, participants reflected positively on the openness and kindness they experienced while speaking with local residents during evangelism.

On the second day of the retreat, participants visited the YEF Macau Center for the first time together, marking a meaningful moment for the fellowship. Located within a residential building near the church, the center is currently used for worship services, Bible study, fellowship gatherings, and ministry activities. Visitors shared encouragement regarding the welcoming atmosphere of the space and its potential to continue serving future ministry and fellowship efforts in Macau.

Participants also reflected on the long history of mission work connected to the building, which had previously been used for ministry and community service purposes for many years. Through the visit, many prayed that the space may continue being used to serve future generations through worship, fellowship, discipleship, and Gospel outreach.

YEF Macau gives thanks for everyone who participated in the Joint Pentecost Retreat and continues praying that the Holy Spirit may continue guiding and strengthening the ministry in Macau. The fellowship also hopes that more students and young people throughout the city may encounter God through Bible study, worship, prayer, and Christian fellowship in the future.

title: YEF Hong Kong Participates in the HK Pentecost Retreat, Experiencing the Mighty Power of the Holy Spirit
excerpt: From May 22–24, YEF Hong Kong participated in a Pentecost Retreat held in Hong Kong under the theme “The Fire of the Holy Spirit, the Fire of Revival.” Throughout the retreat, participants gathered…
paragraphs: From May 22–24, YEF Hong Kong participated in a Pentecost Retreat held in Hong Kong under the theme “The Fire of the Holy Spirit, the Fire of Revival.” Throughout the retreat, participants gathered together for worship, Bible teaching, prayer, and fellowship while reflecting on the meaning of Pentecost and the continuing work of the Holy Spirit in the lives of believers today.

The retreat began Friday evening with a worship service focused on praise and prayer. Throughout Saturday, multiple Bible teaching sessions were held, continuing through the Pentecost Sunday worship service and concluding with a special prayer gathering on Sunday afternoon. The messages centered on the Holy Spirit, spiritual renewal, discipleship, and the mission of believers to continue sharing the Gospel throughout the world.

Many participants shared that the retreat became a meaningful time of encouragement, reflection, and spiritual renewal. During the worship gatherings and Bible studies, attendees reflected more deeply on the work of the Holy Spirit and the importance of living faithfully with renewed purpose and direction. Several participants testified that the messages and prayer times helped them better understand how the Holy Spirit guides, strengthens, and transforms believers in daily life.

One participant shared that the retreat helped them experience the presence of God more personally through worship and prayer, while another reflected on how the messages encouraged them to continue growing spiritually and living with greater faith and commitment. Others also testified that the retreat gave them renewed strength, peace, and motivation to continue pursuing spiritual growth and participating more actively in worship and fellowship.

One of the central themes emphasized throughout the retreat was the Great Commission and the calling for believers to continue sharing the Gospel with the world through the power of the Holy Spirit. Participants were encouraged to move forward not only with personal faith, but also with hearts prepared to serve others, strengthen fellowship, and continue growing as disciples of Christ.

YEF Hong Kong gives thanks for everyone who participated in the retreat and continues praying that the work of the Holy Spirit may continue guiding and renewing the lives of young people throughout Hong Kong. The fellowship also hopes that more students and young adults searching for truth, hope, and spiritual direction may continue encountering God through worship, Bible study, prayer, and Christian fellowship.

title: YEF Orlando Hosts Two-Day Pentecost Retreat Reflecting on the Work of the Holy Spirit
excerpt: On May 23rd, YEF Orlando hosted its Pentecost Retreat at the YEF Headquarters in Sanford, Florida. The two-day retreat focused on teaching, worship, fellowship, and reflection on the work of the Holy…
paragraphs: On May 23rd, YEF Orlando hosted its Pentecost Retreat at the YEF Headquarters in Sanford, Florida. The two-day retreat focused on teaching, worship, fellowship, and reflection on the work of the Holy Spirit, with Day 1 centered on scripture-based instruction, shared experiences, and spiritual growth.

The day opened with a service led by YEF Orlando, beginning with worship, prayer, and preparation for the sessions ahead. The opening message was taught by Pastor Danielle White, who emphasized heart transformation, surrender to God, and the renewing work of the Holy Spirit in the life of believers from Acts 2.

After the opening service, participants were led into Bible study I, which focused on “The Age of the Holy Spirit” and was delivered by Pastor Daija, focusing on John 14:25-31. This session explored the significance of Pentecost in Acts 2 as well, explaining the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, its fulfillment of prophecy, and its ongoing role in empowering believers today. The teaching highlighted how the Holy Spirit equips the church, distributes spiritual gifts, and enables believers to live with boldness and spiritual conviction.

Bible study II, based on Romans 8:26-27, was led by Pastor Rani, focusing on the Holy Spirit’s role in prayer and intercession, especially in moments of weakness. This session emphasized that the Holy Spirit helps believers pray according to God’s will and strengthens them when they do not have the words to pray on their own.

After the studies, participants were encouraged to reflect on the messages and share the grace received. Afterward, a lunch fellowship was held where they continued ruminating on the messages and also shared in fun, Christian icebreaker games, which helped further reflection on the messages. This time then transitioned into activity in which they broke up into teams and played trivia games based on the Word and the Holy Spirit's coming.

Later, Pastor Danielle White returned to lead the third Bible study on Acts 2:42-47, continuing the theme of the Holy Spirit’s work in the believer’s life, reinforcing empowerment, guidance, and spiritual maturity within the church community.

Throughout the day, participants including newcomer, Angel, and committed member, Tamara Hollis, shared reflections in group discussions, expressing how the teachings impacted their understanding of the Holy Spirit. Many highlighted themes such as peace in weakness, spiritual empowerment, and the importance of experiencing the Holy Spirit as a daily presence rather than a one-time encounter. The retreat also included fellowship time, meals including lunch and dinner, and recreational activities such as charades, which helped strengthen relationships and create a joyful atmosphere of community.

The day concluded with a time of prayer and worship, as attendees gathered in gratitude for all that was received throughout the sessions. The retreat ended with a closing prayer asking for continued spiritual protection and growth for those who attended Day 1, that they would hold onto the grace they received and be strengthened in their faith. It was also prayed that those joining on the following day would encounter no distractions or interruptions, but would instead receive even more grace and revelation. A special prayer was lifted for Florida members, that they would be filled and renewed by the Holy Spirit during this retreat, and that the work begun in hearts would continue to grow in power, unity, and spiritual awakening.

title: The Holy Spirit and the Victory of Christ: Branson Pentecost Retreat Continues Through John 16 and the Promise of Truth
excerpt: On May 22, the Pentecost Retreat in Branson, Missouri, continued with Bible Study II as Pastor Anthony shared a message from John 16 centered on the work of the Holy Spirit and the victory of Jesus…
paragraphs:
On May 22, the Pentecost Retreat in Branson, Missouri, continued with Bible Study II as Pastor Anthony shared a message from John 16 centered on the work of the Holy Spirit and the victory of Jesus Christ. YEF members together with Bible study students participated in the joint Pentecost Retreat, gathering in worship, fellowship, prayer, and the study of God’s Word during this meaningful time of spiritual renewal.
Through the study, members and students reflected on Jesus’ words, “It is for your good that I am going away,” and learned why the coming of the Holy Spirit was essential for believers to live by faith and understand the truth of God more deeply.

Focusing on John 16:7–11, Pastor Anthony explained how the Holy Spirit convicts the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment. The message emphasized that the greatest sin is unbelief in Christ, while true righteousness is revealed through Jesus returning to the Father after accomplishing salvation through the cross. Members were also reminded that although believers continue living in a fallen world filled with struggles and spiritual battles, “the ruler of this world” has already been judged and defeated through Christ’s victory.

Continuing through John 16:13, the Bible study highlighted that the Holy Spirit is the Spirit of truth who leads believers into all truth. Pastor Anthony explained that without the Holy Spirit, people cannot fully understand the Word of God or spiritual reality. Reflecting on the disciples’ confession in verses 29–30, members and Bible students were encouraged to move beyond outward belief and grow into genuine trust in Jesus Christ as the One sent from God.

The message concluded with reflection on John 16:33, where Jesus said, “In this world you will have trouble. But take heart! I have overcome the world.” Members were encouraged not to fear suffering, difficulties, or spiritual opposition, but instead to hold firmly to the peace found in Christ and continue walking by faith through the power of the Holy Spirit.

The Bible study ended with prayer for all retreat participants to continue abiding in Christ, growing in truth through the Holy Spirit, and living victoriously in the midst of the world through faith in Jesus Christ.

title: YEF Orlando Continues Campus Evangelism and Bible Study at UCF While Preparing for Pentecost Retreat
excerpt: On May 21, 2026, YEF Orlando continued campus mission activities at the University of Central Florida (UCF) through evangelism outreach and Bible study fellowship with regular students. In…
paragraphs: On May 21, 2026, YEF Orlando continued campus mission activities at the University of Central Florida (UCF) through evangelism outreach and Bible study fellowship with regular students. In preparation for the upcoming Pentecost Retreat, the team set up an evangelism booth on campus while distributing flyers and candies containing Bible verses to students passing by, hoping to encourage conversations about faith and invite more students to participate in the retreat.

During the outreach, P. Rani also continued an individual Bible study on Matthew 5:13–16, reflecting on Jesus’ teaching about believers being the “salt of the earth” and the “light of the world.” Through the study, the student reflected on the relationship between receiving God’s love and naturally desiring to share that love with others. He also shared thoughts about how Christians should seek to live as examples through their lives rather than forcing beliefs onto others, recognizing that a genuine life of faith can inspire people to seek God more sincerely.

YEF Orlando continues praying that his heart may become increasingly open to the Word of God and that he may continue growing spiritually through Bible study, fellowship, and worship. Prayer is also being requested for both his spiritual and physical protection as he continues seeking God more deeply.

Following the individual study, the regular group Bible study continued through Romans 1:18–19 together with students who regularly attend the fellowship. The group also spent time together through a short icebreaker activity that encouraged fellowship and communication among the students.

YEF Orlando continues praying for the UCF mission team, the Bible study students, and the ongoing work of the Gospel on campus. The fellowship also hopes that through the upcoming Pentecost Retreat, many students may encounter the grace of God more deeply and continue growing in faith and community.

title: YEF Global Network Prepares for Pentecost Retreat Through Prayer, Evangelism, and Spiritual Renewal Across the Nations
excerpt: Across the global network of Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF), preparations for upcoming Pentecost Retreat gatherings continue taking place throughout campuses, mission centers, churches, and…
paragraphs: Across the global network of Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF), preparations for upcoming Pentecost Retreat gatherings continue taking place throughout campuses, mission centers, churches, and online fellowships in many nations around the world. Students, ministers, missionaries, and leaders have been working together through prayer, evangelism, Bible study, worship preparation, and fellowship activities with the shared hope that many young people may encounter God more deeply during this Pentecost season.

In various countries and regions, YEF chapters have been actively inviting Bible students, newcomers, and campus contacts to participate in the retreat gatherings. Evangelism teams continue reaching out on university campuses, through online ministry, and within local communities, encouraging students not simply to attend an event, but to experience genuine spiritual renewal through the Word of God, prayer, worship, and fellowship.

The preparation process itself has also become a meaningful expression of unity throughout the international YEF ministry network. Different mission fields continue coordinating outreach efforts, preparing Bible studies and messages, organizing practical logistics, and praying together for students who may be attending for the first time. Many chapters especially hope that the retreat may provide students an opportunity to step away from distractions, worldly pressure, and spiritual isolation in order to seek God more clearly and reflect on their lives and faith.

This year’s Pentecost preparations are closely connected with continued studies through the Gospel of John, Romans, Acts, and teachings related to the Holy Spirit, discipleship, salvation, and the life of the early church. Through these studies, students are being reminded that Pentecost was not merely a historical event recorded in Acts chapter 2, but the beginning of the continuing work of the Holy Spirit through believers across generations, campuses, and nations.

YEF leaders continue emphasizing that the purpose of the Pentecost Retreat is not simply temporary emotional encouragement, but true spiritual transformation that leads to deeper faith, repentance, renewed vision, and greater commitment to Christ. Through worship, fellowship, prayer, and the study of Scripture, the hope is that students may discover clearer direction for their lives while growing stronger spiritually and personally.

Many mission fields are also praying that the retreat gatherings may help raise future disciples, evangelists, Bible teachers, missionaries, and leaders who can continue carrying the Gospel into campuses, cities, and nations. As students from different backgrounds gather together in unity, the retreat serves as a reminder that the church is one body united through Jesus Christ and empowered by the same Holy Spirit.

Throughout the worldwide YEF fellowship, preparations continue with expectation, prayer, and gratitude as outreach efforts expand and more students continue responding to the Gospel. YEF continues praying that during this Pentecost season, many lives may be renewed, strengthened, spiritually awakened, and transformed through the retreat gatherings taking place across the world.

title: Macau YEF Prepares Joint Pentecost Retreat: Evangelism & Seeking the Holy Spirit Through Repentant Prayer
excerpt: Macau Immanuel Church is preparing to hold a joint Pentecost Retreat from May 23–24, 2026, under the theme “The Righteous Shall Live by Faith.” This retreat will mark the first joint gathering…
paragraphs: Macau Immanuel Church is preparing to hold a joint Pentecost Retreat from May 23–24, 2026, under the theme “The Righteous Shall Live by Faith.” This retreat will mark the first joint gathering co-hosted together with OF China, Jubilee Ministries of China, and YEF Macau, bringing believers together in unity to reflect on faith, salvation, and the work of the Holy Spirit.

The retreat is centered on helping participants deepen their understanding of the Gospel through the study of Romans chapters 1–4 while encouraging spiritual renewal, unity in Christ, and growth through the Word of God. Messages during the retreat will be shared by a local Macau Church, a Chinese church leaders, and YEF Macau, while international music fellowship Jubilee Ministries will lead praise sessions along with a special praise and prayer night focused on worship and seeking God together.

In preparation for the retreat, YEF Macau has continued praying earnestly and carrying out evangelism outreach near the Central Library and Macau University. Members have been inviting students and local residents to participate in the retreat, hoping that many people may experience renewal through the Holy Spirit and discover deeper hope, faith, and purpose in God.

A joint planning meeting was held on May 15 as the participating ministries worked together to organize the event and prepare spiritually for the gathering. Through prayer, fellowship, and cooperation, the retreat has already become a meaningful example of unity among believers working together for the Gospel.

YEF Macau gives thanks for the opportunity to co-host this retreat together and continues praying that God may pour out His Holy Spirit abundantly throughout the gathering. The fellowship hopes that everyone attending may experience spiritual revival, renewed faith, strengthened families, and deeper commitment to the mission of Christ through the grace of Pentecost.

title: YEF Hong Kong Continues Growing Spiritually Through Morning Service, Bible Study, and Campus Mission Despite the Rainy Season
excerpt: Despite the persistent rain continuing across Hong Kong in recent days, YEF Hong Kong has continued experiencing God’s grace and encouragement through fellowship, worship, and the study of His Word.…
paragraphs: Despite the persistent rain continuing across Hong Kong in recent days, YEF Hong Kong has continued experiencing God’s grace and encouragement through fellowship, worship, and the study of His Word. Through the work of the Holy Spirit, members have continued growing steadily in faith, and meaningful spiritual changes are becoming increasingly visible in the lives of many brothers and sisters.

Brother James recently completed all of the membership bible study session courses and has continued taking steps forward in his spiritual life. On the morning of May 20, Pastor Andrea taught him from Exodus chapter 1, helping him reflect on God’s guidance and faithfulness throughout history. During this time, Brother James also made the sincere decision to begin regularly attending morning services as part of his continued spiritual growth.

Later that afternoon, Pastor Andrea met with Brother Li Ho-hau at the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), where they studied Romans chapters 14–16 together. After the Bible study, evangelism outreach also continued on the CUHK campus as the Gospel was shared with additional students.

On May 21 at 6:30 a.m., YEF Hong Kong held its morning service, attended by Brother James, Brother Li Ho-hau, and Sister Yanran. For both James and Li Ho-hau, this marked their first time participating in the morning service as new believers. Through the worship and message, they received encouragement and grace and shared their desire to continue growing and being renewed through regular worship and fellowship.

In the afternoon, Pastor Andrea continued teaching Brother Li Ho-hau, focusing on God’s purpose in creation. Through the study, he testified that he desires to love the Lord above everything else in the world and continue growing in faith through the Word of God.

YEF Hong Kong continues praying that each member may remain steadfast in faith, continue growing spiritually through worship and Bible study, and experience deeper transformation through the guidance of the Holy Spirit.

title: Tonga YEF Campus Bible Study Welcomes New Students Through Romans Study and Team Activities
excerpt: On May 19th, YEF Tonga held a Bible study gathering at the University of the South Pacific (USP) Tonga campus, where six students participated, including four first-time attendees. During the…
paragraphs: On May 19th, YEF Tonga held a Bible study gathering at the University of the South Pacific (USP) Tonga campus, where six students participated, including four first-time attendees. During the gathering, the students studied Romans 1:1–17 together, reflecting on the introduction to the book of Romans and the message of salvation through faith in Jesus Christ.

After the Bible study, the fellowship held a Scripture quiz activity in which the students were divided into two groups. The winning team received a small prize packet of biscuits as encouragement. This marked YEF Tonga’s first effort to include interactive fellowship activities alongside Bible study in order to help students engage more naturally with the Word of God and with one another.

The activity helped create a more open, joyful, and welcoming atmosphere among the students, encouraging participation and conversation throughout the gathering. Video highlights from the event were later shared online as part of YEF Tonga’s ongoing outreach and campus ministry efforts.
YEF Tonga continues praying that more students at USP Tonga may come to know the Gospel, grow through Bible study and fellowship, and experience God’s grace personally through the ministry on campus.

title: YEF Macau Strengthened Through Global Ministers Gathering, Moving Forward Toward Pentecost
excerpt: On Wednesday, YEF Macau participated in an online April ministers gathering for the first time with a grateful heart, receiving encouragement, unity, and renewed strength as the ministry continues to…
paragraphs: On Wednesday, YEF Macau participated in an online April ministers gathering for the first time with a grateful heart, receiving encouragement, unity, and renewed strength as the ministry continues to move toward Pentecost.

The gathering began with a sermon based on John 21:3–6, titled, “They Cast the Net, and Now They Were Not Able to Haul It In Because There Were So Many Fish.” The message emphasized the importance of aligning one’s life with the direction of the Lord. Through understanding His love, participants were reminded of the call to repentance, the experience of the cross, and the power of the resurrection at work in their lives.

Following the message, updates were shared on the progress of various ministries, along with testimonies of grace from different regions. These testimonies reflected the continued work of God across nations, encouraging all participants to remain faithful in their calling. Goals and priorities for the coming month were also outlined, with a shared focus on strengthening evangelism, discipleship, and mission development. Updates from regional ministries, including Hong Kong, Macau, and Japan, further highlighted the unity and movement of the global fellowship.

During a time of prayer, a powerful image was shared—three eagles soaring and circling together, and three cords woven into one, strong and united. Even when separated, each remained connected by many strands. This served as an encouragement, reflecting the unity and strength of the ministries as they continue to labor for the next generation. It was also a reminder that the work being carried out is precious in God’s sight and holds significance in reaching and transforming young people.

The three-hour gathering concluded with a time of prayer, lifting up the ministries and the ongoing mission work. Through this time, the YEF Macau minister was strengthened with renewed hope and conviction, moving forward with greater clarity and faith as the season leading to Pentecost continues.

title: YEF St. Louis Cell Group Strengthens Fellowship Through Shared Meal After Service
excerpt: Following the worship service, the mission cell group gathered for a time of lunch fellowship. Students and members came together in a warm and encouraging environment, sharing not only a meal but…
paragraphs: Following the worship service, the mission cell group gathered for a time of lunch fellowship. Students and members came together in a warm and encouraging environment, sharing not only a meal but also meaningful conversation and connection.

This time of fellowship reflected the growing sense of unity within the mission community. As relationships continue to deepen, moments like these serve as an important part of building a strong and supportive foundation where individuals can grow in faith together.

The gathering also highlighted the importance of community in the life of the mission. Beyond services and Bible studies, these shared moments create space for encouragement, mutual care, and a greater sense of belonging among students and members.

Through this continued fellowship, there is a clear sense that God is steadily building and strengthening the community—raising a group that is not only connected through mission, but also through genuine relationship and shared faith.

title: YEF Africa Held Evangelism at University of Nairobi- Kabete Campus
excerpt: On April 15, 2026, YEF Africa carried out an evangelism outreach at the University of Nairobi Kabete Campus. P. Solomon, together with church members, visited the campus with a shared purpose—to…
paragraphs: On April 15, 2026, YEF Africa carried out an evangelism outreach at the University of Nairobi Kabete Campus. P. Solomon, together with church members, visited the campus with a shared purpose—to faithfully share the gospel and build connections with students.

Kabete Campus, known for its programs in Veterinary Medicine and agriculture-related fields, provided a meaningful setting for personal engagement. The team approached students with care, taking time to listen to their thoughts and experiences while sharing the message of the gospel in a clear and approachable way. Through these one-on-one conversations, seeds of faith were planted, and students were invited to reflect on God’s Word and His presence in their lives.

Later that evening, the outreach continued through a Bible study session, where students who had been met earlier were invited to gather and learn more. By God’s grace, two students, Sister Doreen and Sister Abigya, attended the Introduction to the Book of Romans study. During this time, they were introduced to foundational truths of the gospel, opening the way for deeper understanding and continued spiritual growth.

This moment reflects the ongoing commitment of YEF Africa to not only reach students through evangelism but to walk with them through consistent teaching and discipleship. Each connection is seen as an opportunity to nurture faith and guide individuals step by step toward a stronger relationship with God.

YEF Africa continues to lift Sister Doreen and Sister Abigya in prayer—that they may be strengthened in their faith and grow in their understanding of God’s Word. There is also ongoing prayer for all the students who were contacted during the outreach, that the seeds planted in their hearts may take root and lead them to join future Bible studies and fellowship. Through these efforts, there is continued hope that more students will come to know the Lord and be raised as faithful disciples.

title: Lent 2026 Walking the Path of the Cross
excerpt: During this Lenten season, Youth Evangelical Fellowship invites members and students around the world to journey together through The Path of the Cross, a 40-day meditation centered on John 13–19.…
paragraphs: During this Lenten season, Youth Evangelical Fellowship invites members and students around the world to journey together through The Path of the Cross, a 40-day meditation centered on John 13–19. These passages guide us step by step through the final hours of Jesus’ earthly ministry—His love, His suffering, and His sacrifice.

Lent is not merely a time of outward reflection. It is a call to look deeply at the heart of Christ. As the meditation begins with John 13:1, we are reminded that “having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end.” The cross did not begin at Golgotha. It began in love. Even as betrayal, denial, and suffering approached, Jesus loved His disciples to the very end.

Throughout these forty days, we meditate on powerful contrasts: the humility of Christ washing His disciples’ feet, the dispute among the disciples about greatness, the devotion of the woman who broke the alabaster jar, and the tragedy of Judas’ betrayal. Each scene exposes both the depth of Christ’s love and the weakness of the human heart.

Lent invites us to examine ourselves. Are we loving to the end? Are we serving rather than seeking to be served? Are we responding to grace with gratitude, or are we becoming calculative and hardened? The meditations remind us that suffering in Christ is not meaningless. Scripture teaches that suffering produces endurance, character, and hope. When we understand that Christ’s suffering was love poured out completely, we begin to see that true life is found not in self-preservation, but in self-giving.

The Path of the Cross also leads us to consider rebirth. Jesus taught that those who have been washed must continue to wash their feet. In other words, we who have received grace must live in daily repentance and renewal. Lent is a time to return, to cleanse, and to be restored.

For YEF, this season is especially meaningful on our campuses and in our mission fields. As we meditate on Christ’s humility and sacrifice, we are called to reflect that same love in our communities. True leadership in the Kingdom of God is found in serving. True greatness is found in lowering ourselves. True mission flows from love that does not calculate cost.

As we walk these forty days together, may the cross pierce our pride, soften our hearts, and deepen our gratitude. May we not be indifferent observers of Christ’s suffering, but transformed disciples who respond with wholehearted devotion.
And as Easter approaches, may we experience not only the sorrow of the cross, but the joy of resurrection—living as people who have been loved to the end.

title: Last Day of Orientation at the Campus: Set up New Registered Member, Gained Contacts, Bible Studies
excerpt: The final day of Orientation Week at the University of the South Pacific was truly fruitful and encouraging. By God's grace, nearly 500 students visited our booth, and many showed interest in joining…
paragraphs: The final day of Orientation Week at the University of the South Pacific was truly fruitful and encouraging. By God's grace, nearly 500 students visited our booth, and many showed interest in joining our activities and Bible studies on campus.

One of the highlights was Sister Deborah, a third-year student at USP, who officially signed the registration form after attending several Bible studies with Pastor Rachel. She also participated in the first day of Orientation Week services and faithfully assisted at the booth, answering inquiries, welcoming students, and inviting her friends and classmates to join the campus Bible studies. Her enthusiasm and willingness to serve have been a great blessing to the team.

The evangelism team continued to reach out diligently to students around the campus. Through meaningful conversations, two brothers who joined the second Bible study session after connecting with Missionary Susana. They listen in the books of Romans 1. During the conversation, one of the brothers shared that he was born in the Solomon Islands, the hometown of Brother Roy, one of our members. This connection opened the door for warm fellowship and deeper engagement.
In total, two Bible study sessions were held on campus, with four newcomers attending. We thank God for each student who came, listened, and expressed interest in learning more about His Word.

title: YEF Korea Begins Campus Evangelism Ahead of New Semester
excerpt: The YEF Korea Headquarters launched its campus evangelism initiative just one week before the start of the new semester. The staff visited Yonsei University, So-gang University, and Ewha Womans…
paragraphs: The YEF Korea Headquarters launched its campus evangelism initiative just one week before the start of the new semester. The staff visited Yonsei University, So-gang University, and Ewha Womans University. Each of these campuses is near YEF Korea's headquarters.

The staff preached the gospel there, with a particular focus on incoming freshmen. YEF Korea aims to lead 70 newcomers to its upcoming Easter Retreat at OAPC. To achieve this goal, YEF Korea will focus its efforts on both on-campus street evangelism and online evangelism through social network services.
"After overcoming His temptations, Jesus personally sought out and made disciples who would do mission with Him. Likewise, we hope to find potential souls who, like the disciples, will lead many others to the Lord in the future," said the staff involved in the evangelism
'"Come, follow me," Jesus said, "and I will make you fishers of men." At once they left their nets and followed him.' (Matthew 4:19-20)

title: A Testimony of Grace and Renewal at the Asia-Pacific Christmas Retreat in Korea
excerpt: From December 23 to 25, participants from YEF Hong Kong attended the Asia-Pacific Christmas Retreat held in Korea. For some, it was their first time joining a large regional gathering, and over the…
paragraphs: From December 23 to 25, participants from YEF Hong Kong attended the Asia-Pacific Christmas Retreat held in Korea. For some, it was their first time joining a large regional gathering, and over the three days, they experienced God’s grace in deeply personal and transformative ways.

Throughout the retreat, they encountered both inner struggle and the clear movement of the Holy Spirit. As they reflected on God’s Word and listened to the messages, many became aware of areas of self-righteousness and felt conviction over sin. Feelings of guilt and shame led to humbled hearts, opening the way for repentance and renewal. Through this process, they came to better understand the unconditional love of Jesus Christ—a love so complete that it extends even to Judas, who betrayed Him. This realization revealed the depth of God’s love and reminded them how blessed believers are to be loved by such a compassionate Lord.

They were also reminded that God’s love is not based on human merit. The Lord has compassion for sinners and draws near to those who suffer. In times of struggle and weakness, they learned not to withdraw, but to come courageously before the Lord in prayer and supplication, trusting in His mercy and grace.

During the retreat, many became more aware of their own weakness. Reading about the sorrow Jesus experienced when He was rejected by those He loved moved them deeply, especially as they reflected on personal inadequacies. At times, they felt small and unworthy. Yet through encountering Christ, this perspective began to change. In Jesus, they experienced freedom and restoration, recognizing that the Lord removes the chains that bind the heart.

In addition to worship and teaching, they received great grace through serving others. By helping in the cafeteria—washing dishes, mopping floors, and wiping tables—serving in small and unseen ways became an opportunity to follow the example of Jesus Christ, the Servant Lord, who came not to be served but to serve.

This testimony reflects how God works through worship, fellowship, and service to renew hearts and draw His people closer to Him. The experience of YEF Hong Kong participants at the Asia-Pacific Christmas Retreat in Korea stands as a reminder that God’s grace meets believers both in moments of conviction and in faithful acts of humble service.

title: YEF Begins the New Year Grounded in God’s Grace and Kingdom Vision
excerpt: As a new year begins, Youth Evangelical Fellowship is first reminded that everything starts with the grace of God. Apart from the Lord sustaining us, we cannot stand, and apart from His strength, we…
paragraphs: As a new year begins, Youth Evangelical Fellowship is first reminded that everything starts with the grace of God. Apart from the Lord sustaining us, we cannot stand, and apart from His strength, we cannot move forward. As we look back on the past year, YEF does so with humility and gratitude, confessing that every fruit borne, every step of growth taken, and every moment of protection experienced came not from human effort, but from God alone. With this posture of dependence, YEF enters the new year trusting fully in His leading.

This year opens at a significant moment in history. Change is accelerating across societies, cultures, and nations, and the pace of transformation continues to increase. In times such as these, God’s people are called to discern clearly where history is heading. Scripture teaches that history is neither random nor directionless. All history before Christ prepared the way for His coming, and all history after Christ moves toward the fulfillment of God’s kingdom. The future is not shaped merely by human plans or global forces, but unfolds according to God’s sovereign purpose.

Jesus Christ came not only to save individuals from sin, but to reveal the heart of God and to begin the work of God’s kingdom on earth. Through Christ, God made Himself known, and through His teachings—especially the parables of the kingdom—He revealed how God’s reign advances within history. The kingdom does not begin with outward power, visibility, or noise. It begins quietly in the heart, through faith in the Word, and grows steadily as lives are transformed by God’s truth.

Because of this, YEF encourages its members to return continually to the foundations of faith. God’s kingdom advances when His Word is faithfully planted, when hearts become good soil, and when believers live obediently and faithfully where God has placed them. There may be opposition, delays, or seasons of uncertainty, but God remains patient, faithful, and sovereign. In His time, truth and falsehood are revealed, and His purposes move forward without failure.

As the year unfolds, YEF moves ahead with both confidence and responsibility. This is a season to deepen our understanding of God’s Word, to remain filled with the Holy Spirit, and to live with a clear awareness of sin, righteousness, and judgment. With hearts devoted to God and lives shaped by His truth, YEF continues its journey toward the fulfillment of God’s kingdom, trusting that the Lord Himself will lead every step of the way.

title: YEF China December Outreach Update: Proclaiming the Gospel Throughout the Christmas Season
excerpt: As YEF China continues to press forward toward the Christmas 2025 vision, proclaiming the good news of the gospel far and wide, our ministers remained faithful in evangelistic outreach throughout the…
paragraphs: As YEF China continues to press forward toward the Christmas 2025 vision, proclaiming the good news of the gospel far and wide, our ministers remained faithful in evangelistic outreach throughout the entire month of December.

Following a consistent daily rhythm, ministers spent their mornings connecting with seekers online, intentionally looking for hearts that were open and longing, and sharing the good news of the gospel through digital platforms. In the afternoons, they stepped out into the cold winter air to meet people face to face, engaging with nearly 200 individuals and sharing the joyful message of the Lord's coming.

As Christmas approached, the pace of outreach did not slow. Instead, our ministers moved forward with even greater resolve and determination to reach souls. Though the winter winds were cold, their hearts remained warm, strengthened by God's love. The gospel message they carried brought warmth, hope, and light to many during this season.

This month served as a powerful reminder that the message of Christmas is not only something to celebrate, but something to proclaim. YEF China is deeply grateful for the prayers and support of our partners and supporters, and we invite you to continue standing with us in prayer as we trust God to prepare hearts and draw many to Himself.

title: YEF 2025 Christmas Retreat: A Time of Reflection, Worship, and Renewal
excerpt: From December 23–25, 2025, YEF joyfully hosted its annual Christmas Retreat, bringing together members, co-workers, and new friends for a weekend of worship, Bible study, fellowship, and spiritual…
paragraphs: From December 23–25, 2025, YEF joyfully hosted its annual Christmas Retreat, bringing together members, co-workers, and new friends for a weekend of worship, Bible study, fellowship, and spiritual reflection centered on the miracle of Christ’s birth.

The retreat began with a reverent worship service, exploring the mystery of the Incarnation through passages from John and Matthew. Pastor Rani highlighted the journey of the Magi, emphasizing the contrast between those who recognized Jesus as the true King and those who remained spiritually unaware. She encouraged participants to approach Christmas with gratitude and humility, reflecting on God’s grace that allows hearts to receive the Light of the world. The opening service also included meaningful moments of prayer, worship songs, and quiet reflection, setting a thoughtful tone for the days ahead.

Throughout the weekend, participants engaged in interactive and creative activities designed to foster connection and spiritual growth. Icebreakers, games, and symbolic exercises such as a “Light versus Darkness” activity encouraged discernment, teamwork, and reflection on biblical truths. A gingerbread house-building competition and a Christian edition of “Imposter” brought joy, laughter, and fellowship, balancing fun with thoughtful engagement.

Bible studies were a central part of the retreat, led by Pastors Danielle, Rani, and Bri’Daija. Sessions explored the birth of Jesus, the gifts of the Magi, the humility of the manger, and the prophetic fulfillment of God’s promises. Participants reflected on themes such as obedience, faith, humility, and discernment between true and false kingship. Special attention was given to John the Baptist’s role in preparing the way for Christ, highlighting God’s use of ordinary people to accomplish extraordinary purposes. Discussions encouraged attendees to live out their faith with intentionality, embracing their own roles as witnesses to God’s truth and love.

Worship and prayer were interwoven throughout the retreat, with participants lifting hearts in praise, sharing reflections, and receiving encouragement and clarity about their spiritual journeys. Meals and fellowship provided additional opportunities to strengthen community, as participants shared stories, insights, and laughter, forming bonds that reflected the love and unity of Christ.

The retreat concluded with a powerful closing service led by Pastor Danielle White, focused on the theme “The Word Became Flesh and Dwelt Among Us.” Through Scripture readings, prayer, and worship, attendees were reminded that the true gift of Christmas is not material, but the eternal life offered through Jesus Christ. The weekend ended with a shared meal and a screening of the film David, reinforcing the retreat’s themes of faith, obedience, and God’s purpose.

Overall, the 2025 YEF Christmas Retreat was a time of spiritual renewal, thoughtful reflection, and joyful fellowship. Participants left encouraged, inspired, and reminded of the true meaning of Christmas—the gift of Jesus Christ, the Light of the world, dwelling among us.

title: YEF Macau Is Developing Its Campus Fellowship Under the Collaboration of UMSUCF
excerpt: The University of Macau (UM) is the largest public university in Macau (More than 60% students are from mainland China)  and maintains close ties and cooperation with the mainland government and…
paragraphs: The University of Macau (UM) is the largest public university in Macau (More than 60% students are from mainland China)  and maintains close ties and cooperation with the mainland government and universities. As a result, regulations regarding evangelism and gatherings on campus have been tightened. Apart from UMSUCF-the only officially recognized Christian fellowship under the university's student union-no other Christian organizations are permitted to evangelize or hold fellowship gatherings on campus.

Facing these challenges, Minister Agnes prayed fervently, thank God for answering her prayers and opening a new path for YEF through holding joint prayer meetings among different fellowships and churches at the University of Macau, as well as by participating in UMSUCF's new executive committee election.

First, through organizing a joint prayer meeting at the University of Macau, YEF came into contact with Helen (Summer), a staff of the Macau Student Evangelistic Fellowship (FCS), which has long supported UMSUCF. God worked through her, and she suggested that YEF and UMSUCF could collaborate by holding fellowship gatherings together at UMSUCF's venue, taking turns leading the preaching, Bible studies and discussions.

Agnes also attended the new executive committee election of UMSUCF and met the five newly elected members. She was also grateful for the opportunity to meet with Pastor Lo, the director of FCS, to confirm our collaborative relationship. He mentioned that Christians currently make up less than 1% of Macau's population and expressed hope that more students would join UMSUCF gatherings. He also welcomed support from other fellowships to help UMSUCF grow and suggested further meetings to discuss collaboration.

Give thanks and praise to God for His wonderful works and good purposes. Also ask for your prayers-that YEF may follow God's will, and that He may protect and guide both sides in this cooperation, so that more precious souls may be brought to the Lord.

title: STL Mission Center Christmas Fellowship Brings Grace and Joy
excerpt: On Dec 13th, St. Louis Mission Center held its early Christmas Fellowship, a joyful evening filled with worship, reflection, and fellowship in Christ.
paragraphs: On Dec 13th, St. Louis Mission Center held its early Christmas Fellowship, a joyful evening filled with worship, reflection, and fellowship in Christ.

The atmosphere was filled with joy and gratitude as members lifted their voices in worship to celebrate the birth of Jesus. Pastor Isaiah Li then shared a message from Matthew 2 about the birth of Jesus Christ. He led everyone to meditate deeply not only on the story of Christ's birth, but also on Jesus Christ as truly the Lord and Savior to each believer today. Students were touched by the message and found renewed faith and peace in the Lord.

Following the message, everyone joined the potluck dinner, sharing food, testimonies, and warm fellowship together. The room was filled with laughter, encouragement, and love, as members expressed their gratitude for the blessings of the past year.
We give glory to God for His faithfulness and pray that His light will continue to shine through the students' lives in the coming new year.

title: YEF Launches Pre-Retreat Fellowship Ahead of 2025 Christmas Retreat
excerpt: As Christmas approaches, YEF is joyfully preparing for this year’s Christmas Retreat, which will be held from December 23rd to 25th. This annual gathering is a precious time for members to step away…
paragraphs: As Christmas approaches, YEF is joyfully preparing for this year’s Christmas Retreat, which will be held from December 23rd to 25th. This annual gathering is a precious time for members to step away from the busyness of the season, meditate deeply on the meaning of Christ’s birth, and draw closer to God together. To help our members enter the retreat with hearts already softened, strengthened, and spiritually awakened, YEF is planning a smaller pre-retreat fellowship series beginning next week.

This short, mid-week program will serve as a warm-up to the Christmas Retreat—a simple but meaningful space for fellowship, reflection, and preparation. While the retreat itself will carry deep messages and worship, these days beforehand are meant to gently guide members back into a posture of devotion and joyful expectation. Participants may include regular members like Rachel, Korri, Amia, and potentially Celeste, if she is in town and able to attend with transportation. Seminole students are also welcome to join, depending on their holiday schedules. Others, such as Noah, may already be back home for the break, but the door remains open for all who are available.

Rather than an intensive set of sessions, this pre-retreat time will resemble a light version of the Bible camp held during the summer. The focus will be on preparing the heart, not overwhelming the schedule. Possible meeting days include Wednesday to Friday, shaped flexibly around each student’s availability. Each gathering may include:

A short, reflective Bible study
 A time of prayer and sharing
 Simple fellowship activities or going out together
 Space for deeper conversation and personal check-ins
 Encouragement toward spiritual readiness for Christmas

Our hope is to create an environment where students can breathe, reconnect, and enter the retreat already attuned to God’s voice. So as we prepare for these meaningful days, we turn to Scriptures that remind us why the birth of Jesus remains the center of our faith and the source of our joy.

The YEF Christmas Retreat has always been a time of spiritual renewal, deeper understanding of the gospel, and joyful fellowship. By dedicating a few days before the retreat to prepare our hearts together, we pray that each member can enter December 23rd–25th with peace, focus, and a sense of anticipation for what God will reveal.

As we walk toward Christmas, may God grant each participant a heart that is open, soft, and eager to receive the fullness of Christ’s grace. Through these moments of fellowship, prayer, and reflection, may every student rediscover the wonder of Emmanuel—God with us.

title: YEF Tonga Holds Grace-Filled Bible Study with Newcomers
excerpt:
From the left : Susanna, Palolo, Lose, Olivia
In Tonga, a meaningful step in the growth of Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) took place as a small group gathered for a Bible study filled with grace…
paragraphs:
From the left : Susanna, Palolo, Lose, Olivia
In Tonga, a meaningful step in the growth of Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) took place as a small group gathered for a Bible study filled with grace and new beginnings. Two newcomers joined a local member for the session, marking a moment of connection that began through what seemed like a casual meeting—but was clearly guided by God’s hand.

The Bible study was led by Missionary Susanna Liu, who taught from Romans 1:1–17, a passage that introduces the message of the Gospel and the power of faith. The meeting took place in an office at Tonga High School, providing a simple but heartfelt setting for reflection and learning.

The two newcomers, Olivia and Lose, were introduced to YEF through Palolo, a native member who has been faithfully serving in the local mission. The three met while working together on the legal registration of the fellowship in Tonga, and through their conversations, Olivia and Lose expressed a desire to study the Bible together.

During the study, both newcomers shared how deeply the message touched their hearts. Lose said that the phrase “by faith” resonated with her, helping her realize that God’s love is not based on personal performance but freely given through faith. She shared that she had often felt distant from God for not living up to her own expectations, but through this study, she felt encouraged to open her heart and receive God’s unconditional love.

Olivia also shared that she was moved by the discussion on sanctification—the process of growing spiritually. She reflected that following Christ is not something believers do alone; it is part of carrying out the Great Commission, the call to share the Gospel with others. As Christians serve in this mission, they are continually renewed and refined in their faith.

For Palolo, this gathering was an answered prayer. She expressed deep gratitude that after praying for so long, God had finally opened the way for more Tongans to join in Bible study. She shared that she was reminded again that it is through faith—not human effort—that people draw near to God.

After the study, Missionary Susanna spent time learning more about the two women. Lose, who attends a local Tongan church, said this was her first time joining a Bible study. She shared that the message was deeper than anything she had heard before and that she now wanted to study the Word more carefully. Her younger sister, a student at the same school, also has a strong interest in learning more about the Bible.
Olivia, who comes from the Free Wesleyan Church—Tonga’s largest Christian denomination—also expressed great joy in studying Scripture together and looked forward to continuing.

Missionary Susanna noted that both women showed an impressive understanding of the Bible and a genuine eagerness to grow in faith. As the missionary prepares to leave Tonga, both newcomers expressed their hope to continue studying together daily.

This small but faith-filled group stands as a beautiful testimony to how God works in unexpected ways—turning everyday encounters into opportunities for transformation.
