The YEF Tonga team prays that this fellowship will continue to grow stronger in the Word, becoming like a mustard seed that grows into a great tree, drawing many more people to experience the grace and love of God.

title: YEF Continues to Build New Connections and Grow Faith at Seminole State
excerpt: Members of Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) visited the campus of Seminole State College with a heartfelt desire to share the Gospel and connect with students seeking deeper purpose and faith.…
paragraphs: Members of Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) visited the campus of Seminole State College with a heartfelt desire to share the Gospel and connect with students seeking deeper purpose and faith. Motivated by the hope of bringing even one person closer to Christ, the group stepped out in faith to engage with students and introduce them to the message of God’s love and salvation.

Throughout the outreach, the YEF members spoke with many students, offering friendly conversation, prayer, and invitations to learn more about the Bible. Several students showed interest and shared their contact information to stay connected. One memorable moment occurred when YEF mission volunteer Ruth held an impromptu Bible study with a student named Gianna, who expressed genuine curiosity about faith and Scripture.

The team also took time to pray for the campus and for the hearts of the students they met that day. Later, they gathered for a Bible study focused on Romans 8:18–27, which reflects on the hope and glory that await believers despite present struggles. The discussion encouraged everyone to hold firmly to faith, trusting in God’s plan and the promise of His kingdom.

Among the participants were returning students Cam, Max, Sirena, Rachel, Marlanda, Dylan, and Amia, as well as a newcomer, Madison, who shared her excitement to continue attending future sessions. The group’s warm fellowship and thoughtful discussion created an atmosphere where both new and returning members could deepen their understanding of God’s Word together.

As the outreach concluded, the students received an invitation to join a fellowship gathering at the University of Central Florida, opening new opportunities for connection and collaboration with other Christian students in the area.

YEF continues to pray for the students at Seminole State College—that they may be strengthened in faith, protected in their daily lives, and continue to grow in a meaningful relationship with Christ. May the seeds planted through this outreach bear lasting fruit and inspire more young people to seek the truth and hope found in God’s Word.

title: YEF Worldwide Prepares for General Assembly with Renewed Passion and Purpose
excerpt: As the countdown to the upcoming General Assembly begins, Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) chapters across the globe are pouring their hearts into the final stretch of the year’s mission efforts.…
paragraphs: As the countdown to the upcoming General Assembly begins, Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) chapters across the globe are pouring their hearts into the final stretch of the year’s mission efforts. With less than a week remaining before the worldwide gathering, members are dedicating themselves to tireless outreach, deeper discipleship, and bold acts of faith—sharing the Gospel and transforming lives one soul at a time.

YEF is a Christian youth organization dedicated to guiding young people in faith and service through Bible study, leadership training, and global mission work. Across every continent, YEF members are living out this calling—offering their time, talents, and energy to advance the message of hope found in the Word of God.

In the Pacific Islands, a new chapter has been officially established in Tonga, marking a significant milestone in YEF’s mission expansion. The newly formed group has already begun holding Bible studies and fellowship gatherings, laying a strong foundation for what is expected to become a vibrant community of young believers. The Tonga chapter reflects both the growing reach of YEF’s mission and the hunger for spiritual truth among youth around the world.

In St. Louis, Missouri, a new vision is also taking shape. Two individuals have stepped forward with a shared desire to form a YEF chapter in their city. With Bible study sessions already underway, they are prayerfully working toward building a sustainable fellowship rooted in faith, discipleship, and community outreach. Leaders are supporting the effort as the group seeks to raise committed members and future leaders.

In fact, across the United States, existing YEF chapters continue to focus on evangelism, education, and nurturing members into devoted disciples through consistent Bible study and prayer. Each group aims to strengthen young people’s faith, character, and sense of purpose as they grow together in the Word.

In Romania, YEF has seen an inspiring surge of outreach, with over 200 individuals evangelized in recent months. The local leader continues to teach and guide students, addressing not only questions of faith but also personal challenges and misconceptions about the Gospel. Despite obstacles, the chapter is witnessing lives being transformed and renewed through the light of truth.

Meanwhile, in Ethiopia, YEF’s chapter in Hawassa is fostering spiritual growth and leadership development among young believers. Weekly gatherings are filled with worship, prayer, and Bible study as members prepare to become future leaders who will continue spreading the message of Christ within their communities.

Across the Asia-Pacific region, YEF chapters remain steadfast in their mission—teaching, mentoring, and training students to build unshakable faith. In regions rich with cultural and spiritual diversity, these chapters are planting seeds of hope and truth that continue to grow and bear fruit.

As YEF’s global community prepares to gather for the General Assembly, every chapter’s work—whether large or small—contributes to the shared vision of bringing the Gospel to the nations. These final days before the Assembly are filled with prayer, gratitude, and renewed determination to reach even more hearts with God’s Word.

With the finish line in sight, YEF members press forward together—hearts aligned with God’s purpose, hands committed to the mission, and eyes fixed on the hope of transformation. Each soul reached and every life touched stands as a living testimony to the enduring power of faith and the boundless grace of God.
Pictured here : Chapters in Ethiopia, New York, Tonga, Korea, Romania, St. Louis, and Orlando

title: General Assembly 2025
excerpt: On October 29th, the Annual General Assembly of the World Olivet Assembly (WOA) brings together mission and ministry representatives from across the globe to celebrate God’s blessings, share in…
paragraphs:
On October 29th, the Annual General Assembly of the World Olivet Assembly (WOA) brings together mission and ministry representatives from across the globe to celebrate God’s blessings, share in fellowship, and set the vision for the year ahead.
For Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF), this gathering is a vital opportunity to reflect on the growth of campus mission worldwide and to strengthen unity with the wider body of Christ. As YEF continues to expand its presence on universities, the Assembly provides a space to align with global partners, discuss new strategies, and renew commitment to the calling of raising young leaders for the Gospel.

Through this united effort, YEF remains focused on its mission: to reach students with the Word of God, to build strong communities of faith on campuses, and to raise a generation dedicated to Christ and His Kingdom.

title: The Power of Fellowship on University Campuses
excerpt: On every campus lies an incredible opportunity—not only for academic growth, but also for spiritual fellowship and the deepening of faith among believers. YEF Headquarters continues to encourage and…
paragraphs: On every campus lies an incredible opportunity—not only for academic growth, but also for spiritual fellowship and the deepening of faith among believers. YEF Headquarters continues to encourage and support on-campus activities, recognizing them as a vital step in fulfilling the mission of reaching and leading students with the Gospel.

One of the most meaningful aspects of student ministry is the cultivation of warm, intentional fellowship. When students gather for Bible studies, prayer meetings, or simple times of connection, a unique space is created where grace flows and lives are quietly transformed. In these small yet powerful moments, hearts are opened to God and His Word.

Group Bible studies especially play a central role in campus mission. Surrounded by peers on the same journey of faith, students find a sense of belonging and openness. Honest conversations, thoughtful questions, and shared spiritual insights allow the Word of God to take deeper root. Within this atmosphere of trust and care, many experience the love of Christ in a tangible way.

Fellowship is far more than a social activity—it is an expression of Christ’s love within His body. When students unite in His name, their community becomes a living testimony. Newcomers are often drawn not only by the teaching, but also by the warmth and authenticity of the fellowship.

The mission on campus is not carried by one individual alone, but by the collective witness of believers walking together in faith. As students meet, pray, and grow side by side, they embody the transforming power of the Gospel in visible ways that impact those around them.

For this reason, YEF Headquarters encourages every effort to strengthen campus fellowship. Whether through organized events or simple meetups between friends, each moment of shared grace carries eternal significance. As students build one another up, the light of Christ shines brighter, reaching hearts that may otherwise remain untouched.

In the busyness of campus life, it can be easy to overlook the quiet yet profound power of fellowship. But it remains one of the most effective, Spirit-led ways to nurture faith, encourage growth, and carry forward the mission entrusted to us.
Let us continue to gather, to listen, to study, and to love well—so that grace may abound all the more, and the Gospel may spread to every corner of the campus

title: YEF Romania Member Visits YEF HQ : More Members to Students Visiting the Intl HQ
excerpt: Ilinca from YEF Romania recently traveled to the Youth Evangelical Fellowship International Headquarters in Florida, where she was warmly welcomed by YEF HQ members and local staff. Her visit became…
paragraphs: Ilinca from YEF Romania recently traveled to the Youth Evangelical Fellowship International Headquarters in Florida, where she was warmly welcomed by YEF HQ members and local staff. Her visit became a meaningful moment of connection between the mission field in Romania, the work at headquarters, and the wider global family of the church.

P. Danielle guided Ilinca on a tour of the headquarters property, sharing not only its history but also the vision that continues to shape YEF’s ministry today. She explained how the property has long been a place for fellowship, training, and preparing future leaders who will take the Gospel into universities and nations around the world.

For Ilinca, this experience was both encouraging and eye-opening. Coming from Romania, where evangelism and Bible study are steadily growing, she was able to see firsthand the foundation and resources that support YEF’s global mission. It reminded her that each local chapter’s work is part of a much larger story of God’s plan for young people worldwide.

Ilinca reflected on her visit, sharing:“Even though it still feels kind of surreal for me to be here, I am so grateful to God for being here in the central point of the ministry I serve in and have been a part of for over two years now. Finally visiting the country that indirectly contributed to my faith—bringing me to the light, to real Christianity back in 2020—is amazing. God works in such incredible ways and He deserves all the praise. I thank Him for each and every person I have met so far, and I look forward to finding even one lost sheep on campus before I return to my country. May God work amazingly during this time!”

The visit left both Ilinca and YEF HQ members inspired to continue strengthening the bond between headquarters and local chapters. As more students and leaders engage in training, prayer, and fellowship, YEF moves forward in its mission—to raise a generation of young leaders devoted to Christ and to the spread of the Gospel.

title: YEF Orlando Hosts First General Body Meeting at the University of Central Florida
excerpt: On September 10, 2025, YEF Orlando at the University of Central Florida (UCF) held its first general body meeting of the new school year. Now entering its second year as a registered student club,…
paragraphs: On September 10, 2025, YEF Orlando at the University of Central Florida (UCF) held its first general body meeting of the new school year. Now entering its second year as a registered student club, YEF Orlando continues its mission of reaching students with the Word of God and providing a place of fellowship, growth, and transformation.

The meeting, initiated by student leader Tamara, brought together around 14 students for a time of worship, learning, and connection. The evening began with a lively icebreaker where participants introduced themselves, shared their backgrounds, and expressed their hopes for Bible study this semester.

Pastor Rani gave a short but powerful message from Romans 3, reminding students of God’s unchanging faithfulness and His desire for each of us to grow in His grace. Tamara then introduced the club’s mission and vision, sharing plans for upcoming retreats, trainings, and regular Bible studies. She encouraged everyone to walk diligently in faith and to embrace this year as a journey of spiritual growth and renewal.
Students were deeply moved by the study and shared their reflections:

Aida: “The Lord will never hope for your downfall. He always has open arms, but we shouldn’t take His grace for granted. Romans 3:3–4 reminded me that even though we are simply human, God has chosen us and given us His love.”
Tyrissa: “God’s grace doesn’t give us the right to keep sinning. Instead, I strive to grow stronger in Him. Romans 3:3–4 shows me that God is forever faithful, no matter what.”
Derrick: “God’s truth stands even if everyone were against Him. He doesn’t need me to fulfill His promises, but I need Him every day. Romans 3:4 and Psalm 51:4 stood out to me.”
Jairen: “God is just and good. He doesn’t plan our pain, but He can use even our brokenness for good.”

Following the study, students enjoyed fellowship over pizza and received free YEF notebooks. Several new students, invited by a past participant of YEF’s mission training, also joined and expressed excitement to be part of future activities.

YEF Orlando is thankful for what God is doing on campus and asks for continued prayers for the students who joined this first meeting—that they may be strengthened in their faith and walk closely with Christ. The club looks forward to steady growth this semester and remains committed to sharing the Gospel at UCF, reaching out “one more soul” at a time.

title: By God’s Grace, Romans Bible Study Launches in Pakistan Through Member Efforts
excerpt: By the grace of God, a new Bible study series on the Book of Romans has officially begun in a church in Pakistan through the efforts of YEF member, Anoosh. This marks a meaningful step in…
paragraphs: By the grace of God, a new Bible study series on the Book of Romans has officially begun in a church in Pakistan through the efforts of YEF member, Anoosh. This marks a meaningful step in strengthening the presence of the mission in the country and sharing the Word of God with young people who are eager to learn.

The first sessions took time to carefully explain the study material, but with patience and dedication, the group was formed to guide the lectures. By God’s blessing, more than 20 young students joined the study, showing a genuine hunger for truth and a desire to deepen their understanding of Scripture.

Anoosh and the local team are prayerfully committed to nurturing these students, helping them to build a solid foundation in faith and to grow in their walk with Christ. The hope is that this will not only strengthen the individual students but also expand the mission outreach in Pakistan.

YEF invites everyone to continue praying for the success of this mission—that the Bible studies will bear lasting fruit, that young lives will be transformed, and that the light of the gospel will spread powerfully throughout Pakistan.

title: Devotional: Humility, Sovereignty, and Perseverance in Christ
excerpt: Scripture:“Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility value others above yourselves.” – Philippians 2:3
paragraphs: Scripture:“Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility value others above yourselves.” – Philippians 2:3

When we look at the stories of Cain and Abel, Jacob and Esau, or even the jealousy Paul faced from his fellow Jews, we see a common thread: envy and pride often breed conflict. This reflection reminds us that behind anger or resentment lies a deeper struggle with humility. Sin does not begin with the act itself—it begins with a heart that resists surrender to God.

Humility is not weakness; it is strength under God’s control. When we view the Old Testament through the fulfillment of Christ, we see how the law and the prophets always pointed toward reconciliation and mercy. Jesus, who had every right to judge, instead chose to forgive. This is the path He calls us to walk.

Reflection:God’s sovereignty means He is in control, even when life feels unfair. Jacob, though younger, received the promise; Abel’s offering was accepted while Cain’s was not. These stories can stir up questions of fairness, but they also remind us: God’s plan is higher than our own understanding. Our role is not to compare but to trust. True goodness is shown in how we respond—in choosing peace over bitterness, reconciliation over division.

Paul’s perseverance in Berea and beyond shows us the cost of this faith. He faced jealousy, riots, and opposition, yet he pressed on. Why? Because he trusted the One who called him. His mission was not dependent on human approval but on God’s will.
Application:
When envy arises, pause and ask: Am I trusting God’s plan, or comparing myself to others?
When anger stirs, pray: Lord, give me humility to respond with peace and wisdom.
When opposition comes, remember Paul in Berea: perseverance in Christ is never in vain.

Prayer:Heavenly Father, teach me to walk in humility, laying aside envy and pride. Help me to see Your sovereignty in my life and to trust Your goodness even when I do not understand. Strengthen me, like Paul, to persevere in faith, and fill me with Your Spirit to reflect Your love in all I do. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

title: YEF Concludes August Retreat with a Call to Overcome Evil with Good
excerpt: On August 24, Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) concluded its four-day August Retreat with a closing service in the YEF Chapel. The gathering was filled with heartfelt worship, deep reflection on…
paragraphs: On August 24, Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) concluded its four-day August Retreat with a closing service in the YEF Chapel. The gathering was filled with heartfelt worship, deep reflection on Scripture, and meaningful fellowship among members united by a shared passion for God’s mission.

Pastor Danielle White delivered a Spirit-led message that wove together multiple biblical passages to challenge and inspire attendees toward authentic Christian living. Her sermon focused on Romans 12:14–21, emphasizing the radical command to bless those who persecute us. She connected this teaching with Matthew 5:43–45, where Jesus calls believers to love their enemies and pray for those who oppose them.

“While retaliation may feel natural—‘an eye for an eye’—Christ calls us to something higher,” Pastor Danielle said. “He calls us to forgiveness, compassion, and a reflection of God’s mercy toward all.”

To illustrate God’s relentless love, Pastor Danielle turned to Luke 15, the parable of the lost sheep, reminding the congregation that God’s heart beats for those who are wandering or excluded. Quoting 1 John 4:8, she declared, “God is love,” and urged the community to extend that same love beyond the church walls—even to adversaries.

Drawing from Proverbs and James, she spoke on the need for wisdom and peace, warning that harboring hatred can block God’s work and lead to spiritual destruction. “True wisdom is not about clever words,” she noted, “but about righteous action—choosing goodness over retaliation.”

Pastor Danielle also reflected on 1 Samuel, recounting how David spared Saul’s life despite opportunities for revenge. David’s restraint, she explained, demonstrated a deep trust in God’s justice rather than human instinct.
Throughout the message, Pastor Danielle called the community to embrace the ethic of Christ’s kingdom: to overcome evil with good, choose grace over vengeance, and trust God’s timing and justice.

The service closed with a heartfelt prayer for strength to live out this calling. Afterward, attendees shared a catered lunch from the local golf club and enjoyed an afternoon of bowling—ending the retreat on a joyful note of fellowship and unity.
This retreat not only strengthened bonds within the YEF community but also renewed their commitment to reflect Christ’s love in every sphere of life.

title: YEF Continues August Retreat with In-Depth Study of God’s Election in Romans 9
excerpt: The YEF August Retreat 2025 opened with a strong spiritual foundation as participants gathered for Bible study and fellowship. General Secretary P. Danielle White led the first session from Romans…
paragraphs: The YEF August Retreat 2025 opened with a strong spiritual foundation as participants gathered for Bible study and fellowship. General Secretary P. Danielle White led the first session from Romans 9:6–13, declaring with Apostle Paul: “It is not as though the word of God has failed.”

Her message reminded us that being God’s people is not about heritage or outward identity but about living by faith and holding firmly to His promises. Through the stories of Isaac, Ishmael, Jacob, and Esau, she emphasized that God’s calling rests not on human effort but on His sovereign grace and love. This teaching challenged the fellowship to walk in humility, gratitude, and obedience as true children of the promise.

In the second Bible study, Bridaija Jones expounded on Romans 9:11–33, addressing the profound question: “Why not?”—why some receive grace while others do not. She showed that salvation depends not on human will but on God’s mercy, pointing to His ultimate plan of reconciliation for both Jews and Gentiles. Drawing from the parable of the vineyard workers and the faith of the Canaanite woman, Bridaija highlighted that true righteousness comes only by faith.

Both sessions called participants to reject spiritual pride, embrace God’s unmerited favor with gratitude, and live boldly in His grace. The teachings inspired deep reflection, awe, and assurance in the truth that salvation is God’s work from beginning to end.

The evening closed with fellowship over dinner and a joyful movie night, deepening bonds within the community. As the retreat continues, we invite you to join us in prayer—for an outpouring of the Holy Spirit, for hearts to be stirred, and for lives to be transformed through God’s Word.

title: YEF 2025 August Retreat Opens with Powerful Message from Romans 9
excerpt: The YEF 2025 August Retreat began with an opening message from Pastor Rani Reid, who set a deeply spiritual tone for the days ahead by preaching from Romans 9:1–5. Pastor Reid reflected on the…
paragraphs: The YEF 2025 August Retreat began with an opening message from Pastor Rani Reid, who set a deeply spiritual tone for the days ahead by preaching from Romans 9:1–5. Pastor Reid reflected on the profound heart of the Apostle Paul, who expressed unceasing anguish and a willingness to sacrifice himself for the salvation of his people.

Romans chapter 9, Pastor Reid explained, marks a turning point in Paul’s letter—shifting from the assurance of God’s inseparable love in chapter 8 to Paul’s tearful confession of sorrow for Israel. Quoting Paul’s words, “I could wish that I myself were accursed and cut off from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my kinsmen according to the flesh,” Pastor Reid emphasized how Paul’s love revealed a heart aligned with the sacrificial love of Christ.

Paul’s grief, he reminded the retreat participants, was not only personal but rooted in God’s greater history of salvation. Israel had been entrusted with adoption, the covenants, the law, the worship, and the promises, from which Christ Himself came. Yet Paul’s deep sorrow showed his longing for his people to accept Christ, the fulfillment of God’s promise.

Urging everyone to enter the retreat with this same spirit, Pastor Reid called participants to carry a heart willing to bear others’ burdens for the sake of salvation. Just as Paul endured persecution and rejection while holding fast to the mission of Christ, believers today are also called to embrace a love that transcends culture, family, and personal cost.

The retreat will continue with themes from Romans 9–12, exploring God’s election, the unity of His people, and the transformed life of believers. With this foundation, participants are encouraged to seek a deeper understanding of God’s heart and to renew their calling as instruments of His love and reconciliation.
The opening concluded with prayer, asking the Holy Spirit to help all participants take up Paul’s burden and Christ’s love, walking together in faith both during the retreat and beyond.

In total, 16 participants joined, including newcomers Tristen, John, Amia, and Julia. Members Korri, Celeste, and Shannon were also present. Please continue to pray for the retreat, that God’s Word would take root and bear lasting fruit in the lives of all who attend.

title: YEF Welcomes New Mission Trainees and Launches Fall Semester Outreach at UCF
excerpt: On August 19, Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) joyfully welcomed two new mission trainees, Brother Sungil and Sister Yujin, as they joined the ongoing missionary training at the University of…
paragraphs: On August 19, Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) joyfully welcomed two new mission trainees, Brother Sungil and Sister Yujin, as they joined the ongoing missionary training at the University of Central Florida (UCF). Marking the second day of the Fall semester, the fellowship continued to labor faithfully for the Lord, embracing each opportunity to share the Gospel with new students on campus.

In a spirit of creativity and prayerful preparation, the team tried a new outreach method by setting up a booth to promote their upcoming retreat. This fresh approach quickly bore fruit, as several students expressed genuine interest and even signed up to attend. It was a moment of grace that reminded the team how God can use even small acts of faith to open hearts and plant seeds for the future.

Later that day, YEF held its first Bible study of the semester, exploring Romans 1:1–17. The passage proclaims the Gospel as the power of God for salvation, and it resonated deeply with everyone present. The fellowship enjoyed a blessed time of study and sharing, strengthened by the Word and by one another’s faith.

Among those who attended were committed member Tamara, returning student Caleb—who brought along his friend Nia—and newcomers Katrina, Jayden, and Becca. While some gathered for the study, other members remained on campus, continuing to invite students to discover the truth of the Gospel.
Looking ahead, the fellowship is dedicating the coming days to preparing for the retreat, which they pray will be a turning point for many students to encounter Christ personally.

YEF humbly asks for continued prayers—for the preparation of the retreat, for the students who have already committed to attend, and for the mission trainees as they grow in the grace, strength, and love of God. May the Holy Spirit guide each step, and may many be led to the saving knowledge of Christ through this campus mission.

title: YEF China Members Experience Renewal Through Mission in Korea
excerpt: This summer, two missionaries from YEF China joined a short-term mission program in Korea. Each morning, they devoted themselves to studying and meditating on God’s Word, and in the afternoons, they…
paragraphs: This summer, two missionaries from YEF China joined a short-term mission program in Korea. Each morning, they devoted themselves to studying and meditating on God’s Word, and in the afternoons, they went out to freely share the Gospel in public places. Although the experience was at first unfamiliar and challenging, both sisters testified to receiving profound spiritual renewal and release through the outreach.

In China, evangelism often feels constrained by many barriers, but in Korea, they were able to boldly testify to the Gospel without restriction. Their hearts were filled with joy and strength as they experienced the freedom of proclaiming Christ openly. With renewed faith, they now return to China with the hope of continuing to preach with the same Spirit-led passion, reaching many spiritually hungry souls.

At the same time, two other YEF pastors also attended training in Korea, which centered on an intensive study of the Book of Romans. Through this training, they received great spiritual encouragement and renewal. Both were deeply moved once again by God’s immeasurable love revealed in His Word, and they expressed their earnest desire that this flame of love would continue to burn within, bringing lasting transformation in both ministry and personal faith.

After the summer co-workers’ gathering and summer retreat, YEF China has been actively preparing for evangelism in the upcoming school season. The fellowship asks for continued prayers, that God would grant them wisdom and boldness to seize this precious opportunity, to meet many prepared and seeking souls, and to witness a great revival in the new semester.

title: YEF Ethiopia Members Growing in God’s Word
excerpt: By the grace of God, Youth Evangelical Fellowship Ethiopia continues to witness a growing hunger for the Word of God among its members. Recently, Sister Beza joyfully completed studying Romans…
paragraphs: By the grace of God, Youth Evangelical Fellowship Ethiopia continues to witness a growing hunger for the Word of God among its members. Recently, Sister Beza joyfully completed studying Romans chapters 1 through 14, marking an important milestone in her journey of faith.

Through the book of Romans, she came to understand more deeply one of Apostle Paul’s most profound messages: the foundation of the gospel—the righteousness of God revealed through faith in Jesus Christ. Sister Beza’s dedication to carefully studying each chapter has helped her grow in her understanding of salvation, grace, faith, and the call to live a transformed life.

From Paul’s teachings on the universal need for salvation (Romans 1–3), justification by faith (Romans 4–5), life in the Spirit (Romans 8), and the call to Christian living and unity (Romans 12–14), Sister Beza has been able to reflect on these truths and apply them in her daily walk with God.

Leaders of YEF Ethiopia expressed great joy at her progress, emphasizing that this achievement is not only a personal milestone but also a source of encouragement to the whole fellowship. Her journey shows the importance of consistent Bible study and the fruit it bears in strengthening faith and shaping character.

Looking ahead, YEF Ethiopia hopes to register Sister Beza as an official member with the grace of God and prays that her example will inspire many others to go deeper into the Word. Romans 15–16 remain to be studied, and the fellowship looks forward with faith that God will continue to pour His wisdom and grace as they complete the journey together.

Meanwhile, Brother Samuel from Hawassa University Health Campus has been studying Romans chapter 4, where he meditated deeply on justification by grace through faith. Please continue to pray for the mission in Ethiopia, that many faithful members may be raised up across the country.

title: YEF China Launches New Semester Outreach at Peking University
excerpt: On August 18, YEF China officially began its New Semester Outreach at Peking University with a full day of campus evangelism. Eleven YEF coworkers, together with a local YEF pastor from the OFC…
paragraphs: On August 18, YEF China officially began its New Semester Outreach at Peking University with a full day of campus evangelism. Eleven YEF coworkers, together with a local YEF pastor from the OFC Mission Department, devoted themselves from morning until evening to share the gospel with incoming freshmen. By God’s grace, the team was able to make 16 new contacts on the first day.

This outreach was not a sudden effort but the fruit of a month of prayer and preparation. Coworkers gathered regularly to intercede for the campus, brainstorm strategies, and prepare materials. After much discussion, they decided to design customized greeting cards for freshmen, using them as a bridge to open warm conversations and invite students to fellowship. On the afternoon before the outreach, the team prayerfully walked the campus, studied the registration process, and carefully mapped out where coworkers should be stationed in order to meet as many students as possible.

By 7:00 a.m. on the outreach day, crowds of students and parents were already gathering near the subway station and school gates. Brothers arrived early to take their positions by 8:00 a.m., with sisters joining shortly after. Although heavy security presence initially limited large-scale engagement, God provided a way forward. Pastor Yaling coordinated movements across the South and Southwest Gates, where the team found greater freedom to interact.

In the midst of these efforts, the Lord gave moments of divine appointment. While another evangelizing pastor stepped into a nearby KFC to phone coworkers, a parent noticed the words “Love Never Fails” on her T-shirt and asked if she was part of a Christian fellowship. The family turned out to be believers, and their son—a freshman physics major—was joyfully introduced to the YEF team. They exchanged contact information and scheduled future fellowship meetings. This encounter deeply encouraged the coworkers and strengthened their faith to evangelize with even greater boldness. Similarly, Sister Zhuxi connected with a Christian mother who promised to introduce her relatives to the fellowship.

Throughout the day, the team learned that when they stepped forward in faith, God truly gave them the ground beneath their feet. Though some areas felt difficult to approach at first, as coworkers overcame fear and hesitation, they began speaking more freely, distributing cards, and engaging both Christian families and students curious to know more about God.

At day’s end, the outcome did not fully meet their initial prayer target, but the coworkers returned with hearts full of gratitude. What began with fear and uncertainty transformed into peace and release through obedience. On Pastor reflected:“Even though we are weak and limited, as we walk and pray around this campus, the spiritual atmosphere of Peking University is being transformed. Even for the sake of one soul, this is why we are here.”

The YEF China team gives thanks for the Lord’s protection and guidance throughout the first day of the New Semester Outreach. They ask for continued prayers—that more spiritually hungry souls may be found on campuses across China, and that each coworker will keep experiencing God’s leading and the mighty work of the Holy Spirit.
The outreach concluded with a group photo in front of Peking University’s iconic main gate, as coworkers gave thanks for a day filled with grace and God’s presence.

title: Breaking Down the Walls: Lessons from Acts 10
excerpt: Acts 10 paints one of the most pivotal moments in church history—a moment when the gospel truly broke beyond cultural and ethnic boundaries. The story of Peter and Cornelius is more than an ancient…
paragraphs: Acts 10 paints one of the most pivotal moments in church history—a moment when the gospel truly broke beyond cultural and ethnic boundaries. The story of Peter and Cornelius is more than an ancient account; it is a living reminder of how the Holy Spirit orchestrates encounters, dismantles prejudice, and opens doors for the gospel to reach “to the ends of the earth.”

Cornelius, a Roman centurion, was a man of prayer and generosity, yet barred from full fellowship with the Jews because he was a Gentile. Still, God saw his heart. Through a divine vision, Cornelius was led to send for Peter—who, at the very same time, was being prepared by the Holy Spirit to lay aside his deeply ingrained traditions. God’s message was clear: “Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.”

The beauty of this encounter is in its timing. Cornelius’ messengers arrived exactly as Peter was coming out of prayer, pondering his vision. This was no human coincidence—it was the perfect alignment of heaven’s schedule. When they met, Peter crossed a boundary his culture had long forbidden: he welcomed Gentiles into fellowship and entered their home.

This meeting shattered the “dividing wall of hostility” (Ephesians 2:14). Peter declared that God shows no favoritism but accepts anyone who fears Him and does what is right. The Holy Spirit then fell on all who were listening—Gentiles receiving the same gift as Jewish believers—ending the argument that God’s Spirit was reserved only for one group.

For the church today, Acts 10 calls us to live without prejudice, to expect divine appointments, and to keep our hearts open to those God is already preparing. The mission of Christ is never limited by human categories; the gospel is for all nations, all peoples, and all hearts willing to receive it.

The lesson is simple but profound: when we obey the Spirit’s leading, barriers crumble, lives are transformed, and the kingdom of God advances unhindered. May we, like Peter, be ready to say, “I now realize how true it is that God does not show favoritism,” and may we walk boldly into every opportunity to share the good news without discrimination or delay.

title: 2025 Back to School Summer Retreat
excerpt: Youth Evangelical Fellowship warmly invites all students and young adults to join the YEF Summer Retreat 2025, taking place from Thursday, August 21 to Sunday, August 24, 2025—a powerful time of…
paragraphs: Youth Evangelical Fellowship warmly invites all students and young adults to join the YEF Summer Retreat 2025, taking place from Thursday, August 21 to Sunday, August 24, 2025—a powerful time of worship, fellowship, and deep study of God’s Word.

This year’s retreat will be a season of renewal and spiritual breakthrough, with a special focus on Romans 9–16. Through in-depth Bible studies, heartfelt prayer, and joyful praise, participants will be encouraged to grow in their faith, build lasting friendships, and be equipped to live boldly for Christ on their campuses and in their communities.
The retreat will also feature testimonies, group activities, and special sessions to help each attendee discover God’s calling for their life.

Come ready to experience the transforming power of the Gospel and return home with a renewed heart to serve God. Let this be the summer where your faith is strengthened and your vision for the mission is made clear.

title: YEF Orlando Looks to Stabilize Bible Study Students Through Weekly Service Attendance
excerpt: YEF Orlando's evangelism team continued their efforts to bring more students to the Bible studies on the local Seminole State campus. They were able to receive 8 contacts. They found a mixture of…
paragraphs: YEF Orlando's evangelism team continued their efforts to bring more students to the Bible studies on the local Seminole State campus. They were able to receive 8 contacts. They found a mixture of students who are currently interested and some who would be interested once they return from the break. They hope that these students can be protected and guided until they are able to attend the Bible study.

Towards the last few months of their time on the Seminole campus for the summer semester, they were able to find students who wanted to attend the Bible study regularly and come every week. These students were invited to also join the Wednesday service. Last week, Brother Dylan joined for the first time, and now they are praying that Brother Tristan can also join.

Due to a change in her work schedule, Rachel will no longer be able to attend Wednesday service, but graciously, she will have the opportunity to attend Sunday service. For Seminole, the evangelism team has been focusing on getting them to join the services in hopes to continue their growth.
Sister Korri, who recently became a registered member, also has been encouraged to attend Sunday service, so they are also praying she can join this week.

Please continue to pray for all students-that through weekly service attendance and continuous study of the Word of God, they may be stabilized in their faith and grow deeply in their relationship with Christ. Pray that each student may not lose the grace they have received, but instead be firmly planted in the community and guided step by step into a life of devotion and transformation. May the Holy Spirit work powerfully in their hearts during this season of transition and new beginnings.

Student Reflections from the Bible Study:
"The main message I took away from this study is that we have two versions of ourselves: the flesh, which is our earthly body, and our spirit. Our flesh isn't what lives forever, but it determines how our spirit will live for eternity. The verse that stuck with me is 1 Corinthians 15:44. This stood out to me because you often hear about how people live for the flesh and earthly desires, but in the end, it will be your spirit that is raised from the ground-not what you had during your earthly life."
"The message I took from this lesson was to not stress or dwell over physical things, because at the end of the day, everything goes away. One thing that stood out to me was when you said that we have three stages of life: the first in the womb, then life, and death-and you compared the womb to life, which prepares us for eternal life. If we don't prepare rightly in life, we won't necessarily have the right things for heaven and eternity. The flesh is not eternal. One verse that stood out was Matthew 6:25, because it's a reminder that all of this doesn't matter as long as we are following God. All this suffering is temporary, but death, heaven, and being with Him is eternal."

title: Hearts Opened and Lives Transformed in Arizona Mission Field
excerpt: On August 5th, the pioneers of Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) Arizona, Hyewon and Lucy, pressed forward in the mission field with unwavering faith, holding an incredible 11 Bible studies in a…
paragraphs: On August 5th, the pioneers of Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) Arizona, Hyewon and Lucy, pressed forward in the mission field with unwavering faith, holding an incredible 11 Bible studies in a single day. This day of ministry highlights the heart of YEF: to reach, teach, and raise up students with a deep love for God’s Word and a desire to walk in truth.

Hyewon met with several students throughout the day, continuing studies in the book of Romans. Trevor completed Romans 1 and received the Word with humility and openness, eager to grow in his knowledge of God. Nick completed Romans 6 and offered a powerful reflection, connecting passages across Scripture to better understand the Christian journey. He described how Romans 6 grounds us in our identity in Christ—dead to sin, alive in Him—while 1 Corinthians 9:27 reminds us to live with discipline, and John 15:5 anchors it all in our abiding relationship with Christ.

Genesis also studied Romans 6 and found newfound clarity about salvation after wrestling with misunderstanding. She shared openly about her past and expressed a desire to grow in her faith. Please pray that she may become a registered member and join the upcoming St. Louis retreat. Ivana returned to study after a brief illness and reflected on Romans 5, sharing how trials can build character and hope. She quoted 1 Peter 1:6–7 and 2 Corinthians 1:9, expressing how the Word taught her to rely on God, not herself.

Dayton finished Romans 2 and expressed interest in attending the retreat as well, while Hyewon also met Stuard for the first time. Though not yet a believer, Stuard listened to the gospel message with sincerity—an opportunity the pioneer cherished deeply.

Meanwhile, Lucy met with four returning students and welcomed one new participant. In her study with Manuel on Romans 2, he compared the spiritual condition of the Pharisees to how he sometimes memorizes formulas just to pass exams—without truly understanding them. He shared a desire to become a Christian transformed from the inside out.

Later, Aleeah, an online master’s student, began her journey in Romans 1. She opened up about struggles with sin and identity, and received the Word with a humble, seeking heart. Blessing continued with the second half of Romans 1 and reflected deeply on what it means to glorify God and live dependently on Him. She prayed that her heart would never grow proud or self-reliant, but always remain anchored in God’s will.

Jay, studying Romans 3, reflected on the fall of man and free will, realizing that no one is perfect—and that connecting with God comes through faith, not perfection. He expressed a growing desire to live with humility and grace toward others.

Lastly, Lucy met with Bronwen to complete Romans 1. Bronwen thoughtfully engaged with the text, took notes, and opened up about her battle with legalism. She shared that she’s learning to understand God’s grace beyond the pressure to perform or be perfect.

Each of these meetings is a living testimony to the mission and purpose of YEF—to meet students with the Word of God, to walk with them in truth, and to raise them up as disciples. These are not simply one-time conversations; they are moments of encounter that can transform lives forever.

As the week continues, YEF Arizona asks for your prayers. Pray for every student who has heard the Word—that they may feel the love of God personally and powerfully. Pray that the seeds sown would take root, and that many would rise up as faithful, fruitful followers of Christ.

Youth Evangelical Fellowship continues to invite students across the nation to study the Bible and discover a life shaped by faith, guided by Scripture, and grounded in the love of Jesus Christ. If you or someone you know is seeking truth, hope, or community, YEF is here to walk with you.

title: YEF Reaffirms Paul’s Model of Leadership for Sustainable Missions
excerpt: In this new season of global mission, Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) is renewing its focus on a key biblical truth: no missionary is called to labor alone. As seen in the Apostle Paul’s…
paragraphs: In this new season of global mission, Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) is renewing its focus on a key biblical truth: no missionary is called to labor alone. As seen in the Apostle Paul’s relationship with Timothy (2 Timothy 2:2), effective gospel ministry is not built on individual effort but on intentional partnership, spiritual formation, and the passing on of leadership.

Paul’s ministry was never self-centered. His goal was not simply to evangelize, but to build systems and relationships that would continue the work long after he was gone. By investing in others, training them well, and entrusting them with real responsibility, he laid a strong foundation for the Gospel to spread across cultures and generations. His method gave birth to spiritually mature, self-sustaining communities that could grow without constant dependence on outside leadership.

YEF sees this model as essential for the long-term health and expansion of the mission. Rather than relying on a few workers in the field, the focus is shifting toward empowering students and local leaders to rise as future teachers, disciplers, and spiritual shepherds. This approach, often referred to by missiologists as “multiplication-focused mission,” emphasizes leadership development—not merely recruiting volunteers, but forming disciples who can carry the mission forward faithfully. Paul’s leadership handoff was not casual or rushed. He discipled leaders closely in daily life, selecting them with care and training them in both spiritual and practical matters. Authority was not given lightly; it was nurtured through relationship, godly example, and ongoing partnership. Even after handing over responsibility, Paul remained present—guiding, encouraging, and strengthening the ones he had raised up.

At the core of Paul’s model is a vital shift in mindset: the missionary is not the controller of the work, but a catalyst and co-laborer. Tasks are not simply assigned—they are shared through vision, trust, and example. This is the kind of mission YEF desires to build in every chapter, city, and nation. One that is not dependent on one leader’s strength, but one that grows through community, shared conviction, and spiritual reproduction.

In a rapidly changing world, where cultural, technological, and generational dynamics are constantly shifting, Paul’s model remains a timeless blueprint. For YEF, it is not enough to simply reach new students. The greater goal is to equip and entrust them—so they can rise up as leaders, disciple others, and help carry out the Great Commission wherever God sends them.

As we move forward, YEF calls all its chapters and leaders to prioritize this vision: to form people. Invest in relationships. Train intentionally. Entrust wisely. And always, through prayer and shared faith, believe that the mission will multiply through those God raises up.

title: YEF Hong Kong Engages Youth Through Online Evangelism and Uplifting Worship
excerpt: Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) Hong Kong continues to find creative and Spirit-led ways to reach young people in today's fast-paced, digital world. The team is currently exploring and…
paragraphs: Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) Hong Kong continues to find creative and Spirit-led ways to reach young people in today's fast-paced, digital world. The team is currently exploring and experimenting with new forms of online evangelism to meet the spiritual needs of this generation where they are—online.

In a recent effort, Pastor Andrea uploaded six short videos on the WeChat Video Channel, addressing practical and heartfelt topics such as parenting and “Choosing a Life Partner While Single.” These subjects have resonated deeply with young people, particularly in an era where many are searching for guidance on love, relationships, and family. The videos were warmly received, garnering many likes from fellow believers and “little lambs.” Some viewers even reached out privately, offering encouragement, testimonies, and words of affirmation, showing how even short messages can spark meaningful conversations and connections.

On July 27th, YEF Hong Kong also held its Sunday service, where Pastor Philip delivered a powerful sermon from John 11:1-44 titled “If You Believe, You Will See the Glory of God.” The message centered on faith in the midst of impossibility, drawing from the story of Lazarus to inspire attendees to trust in God's power and timing. The worship service provided a time of spiritual refreshing and reflection for all who participated.

As YEF Hong Kong continues to grow in its mission both online and in-person, we ask for your prayers. Please pray for greater outreach through digital platforms, wisdom for the ministers, and open hearts among the youth in Hong Kong. May more lives be touched by the Gospel and see the glory of God in their own journey of faith.

title: YEF Orlando Evangelism Team Sees Fruitful Outreach at Seminole State College
excerpt: Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) continues to witness God’s grace and movement through the ongoing mission efforts at Seminole State College, where the Orlando Evangelism Team—together with…
paragraphs: Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) continues to witness God’s grace and movement through the ongoing mission efforts at Seminole State College, where the Orlando Evangelism Team—together with dedicated mission trainees—has been actively sharing the Gospel and leading students into deeper encounters with God’s Word.

This week marked a meaningful milestone for both trainees, Ruth and Jubilee, as they each led their first one-on-one Bible studies. Jubilee had the joy of teaching Romans 1 to Gary, a student at Seminole State, guiding him through the foundational truths of the Gospel. Similarly, Ruth connected with a student named Michael during morning evangelism, and by God’s grace, they studied Romans 1 together later that day. Their fellowship was so fruitful that Michael agreed to meet again the next morning at 8 a.m. for a follow-up Bible study.

In addition to these individual studies, the team engaged with 11 new students on campus, planting seeds of faith and encouraging spiritual curiosity. A group Bible study was also held, attended by three newcomers and four returning students, along with registered member Racheal. The session centered on Romans chapter 8 and provided a welcoming environment for open discussion and reflection.

After the group study, Heeyeon continued with several individual Bible studies with students who had participated in the group session—Jeremiah, Noah, and Emily. She walked each of them through Romans 1, sharing that they grasped the message with both clarity and spiritual depth.

Trainee Ruth reflected on the experience, saying,
“When we went out to share the Gospel on campus, even though there weren't many people, most of those who were there received us with open hearts; it was truly a grace-filled and interesting experience. It also felt like the mission ministers here have been laying a strong spiritual foundation through evangelism over a long period of time.”
She also shared a deeper realization:
“Bringing someone to God has nothing to do with how well or poorly I can speak. The Holy Spirit is truly the one doing the work, leading us to meet the right person at the right time. This has given me faith that the Holy Spirit is guiding everything... I'm truly thankful for the YEF fellowship that is supporting us in every way... Since everything is prepared, we can now focus fully on the mission... and continue on this journey with light hearts.”
As the Orlando Evangelism Team continues to pour out their hearts in service, we invite you to pray for the team and their mission trainees—for their spiritual growth, protection, and endurance, and especially for the students they meet. May hearts be open, lives be transformed, and God's Word take root on campus and beyond.

title: YEF UCF & SSC Retreat Ignites Reflection and Renewed Faith Among Students
excerpt: The 2025 YEF UCF & SSC Summer Retreat brought together students and members for a time of deep reflection, powerful Bible studies, and a renewed commitment to their walk with Christ. Held with the…
paragraphs: The 2025 YEF UCF & SSC Summer Retreat brought together students and members for a time of deep reflection, powerful Bible studies, and a renewed commitment to their walk with Christ. Held with the purpose of nurturing spiritual growth and unity, the retreat served as a vital time of encountering God's Word and being transformed by it.

Throughout the retreat, participants engaged in rich Bible studies covering themes from the Book of Exodus—spanning topics such as spiritual renewal, the Christian mindset, the sovereignty of God, and the power of love. Below are heartfelt reflections from several attendees who were touched by the messages:

Emmanuel reflected on the need to reshape and renew the mind in faith, much like Moses during his time in Midian. “We are trained in survival by the world,” he shared, “but to follow God, we must abandon that logic and embrace meekness and holiness.” He was moved by the call to discern deeply—to distinguish between time, place, people, and God’s purpose.

Tamara was reminded of God’s unchanging love and faithful provision. She highlighted the image of the cloud by day and fire by night as symbols of God’s intimate care. “Even in trials, God gives us what we need. He wants the best for us and leads us to cry out to Him, not run away.”

Noah saw in the message a clear model for daily Christian life. “The manna and quail taught me the rhythm of walking with God—starting the day with devotion and ending with reflection. Without it, we walk a longer, harder road.”

Rachel emphasized God’s exclusivity and faithfulness. “God alone deserves the top place in our hearts. He is everything we are looking for. He offers us peace and leads us back with love, not condemnation.”

Asa found deep insight in the message about the law and its place in the life of a believer. “It’s not just about knowing Scripture,” he said, “but applying it with wisdom. Like Jethro, we need spiritual discernment that comes from wholehearted understanding.”

Heeyeon expressed her desire to grow deeper in understanding Christ’s love and the theological richness found in Exodus. “From the plagues to the principles of salvation, the book [Exodus] is filled with meaning. I’m grateful to hear these truths from such a young age.”
This retreat served not only as a time of spiritual teaching but also of spiritual awakening. Attendees left with a stronger sense of mission and a deeper desire to live according to God’s Word.

Please continue to pray for all who participated in the YEF UCF & SSC Summer Retreat. May the seeds of grace planted during this time bear lasting fruit as they continue to grow in faith and commit their lives to the Great Commission.
Youth Evangelical Fellowship remains committed to raising up young leaders who are transformed by the Word and empowered to transform the world.

title: YEF Kenya Expands Campus Mission Through Member Initiative at Thogoto College
excerpt: Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) Nairobi continues to expand its mission field through the dedication of its members. On a recent occasion, Brothers Kelvin and James, who serve part-time as…
paragraphs: Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) Nairobi continues to expand its mission field through the dedication of its members. On a recent occasion, Brothers Kelvin and James, who serve part-time as teachers at Thogoto Technical and Vocational College, extended an invitation to all church members to join them in ministering at the school.

This opportunity not only allowed students at the college to hear the gospel but also gave church members a chance to practice and grow in their teaching and evangelism. The members supported each other, shared the Word boldly, and experienced grace through the mutual encouragement that came from fulfilling the Great Commission together.

Through this outreach, the team also learned valuable lessons on how to connect with students, teach the Bible in an engaging and relatable way, and work together in unity for God’s kingdom. It was a time of both giving and growing.

Please continue to pray for Brothers Kelvin and James, and for the mission at Thogoto Technical and Vocational College—that many more students may encounter the transforming power of the gospel, and that God may raise new leaders from this field for His work.

title: YEF UCF & SSC Concludes Three Day Event : Walking the Path of Exodus
excerpt: The 2025 Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) Summer Event was a powerful and Spirit-filled gathering where participants from the University of Central Florida and Seminole State College joined to…
paragraphs: The 2025 Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) Summer Event was a powerful and Spirit-filled gathering where participants from the University of Central Florida and Seminole State College joined to learn deeply about the book of Exodus. Held by the YEF Florida chapter, the occasion brought together members and leaders for a time of deep reflection, biblical study, and joyful fellowship. Through messages, prayer, and community, participants were invited to leave behind worldly distractions and walk more faithfully in God’s calling.

Pastor Rani Reid opened the gathering with a message on the early chapters of Exodus, highlighting the faith of the Hebrew midwives, the protection of Moses, and the power of fearing the Lord. She urged attendees to live with holy boldness and obedience, just as the Israelites did in the face of persecution. Her message set the tone for a retreat focused on spiritual courage and trust in God's guidance.

Throughout the weekend, Bible studies led by Pastor Danielle White and M. Daija explored key moments from Exodus, including Moses' transformation, the Passover, and God’s provision in the wilderness. Participants were reminded of the importance of humility, holiness, and full commitment to the Word. Lessons from the burning bush, the Red Sea, and the giving of the law encouraged all to grow as leaders and remain rooted in God’s promises.

Alongside study and prayer, the retreat included joyful activities like Bible-themed relays and games, helping members bond while reinforcing biblical truths. Reflection times and testimonies brought the group closer, creating space for healing, repentance, and renewed faith. One special highlight was the official registration of a young Bible student, Rachel, marking a joyful step in her journey with Christ.

The retreat concluded with a Sunday service on “Preserving the First Grace,” drawing from the latter chapters of Exodus. Pastor Danielle shared a powerful message on law, grace, and God’s dwelling among His people. As the retreat ended in fellowship, worship, and celebration, participants left with revived hearts and a clear mission: to live boldly for the Gospel.

The YEF 2025 Summer Retreat was a reminder that just as God led His people from Egypt to the Promised Land, He is still leading His church today. With faith, obedience, and unity, YEF continues forward—raising a generation that lives for Christ.

title: YEF HQ Prepares "Walking the Path of Exodus" Summer Retreat
excerpt: As the summer season unfolds, Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) is preparing for what promises to be a pivotal moment of spiritual renewal and outreach: the upcoming summer retreat. With a heart…
paragraphs: As the summer season unfolds, Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) is preparing for what promises to be a pivotal moment of spiritual renewal and outreach: the upcoming summer retreat. With a heart full of prayer and vision, the team is diligently laying the groundwork to ensure that this gathering becomes a transformative experience for all who attend. This year’s retreat, themed "Walking the Path of Exodus," draws inspiration from Exodus 6:8, where God declares, "I will bring you to the land I swore with uplifted hand to give to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob. I will give it to you as a possession. I am the Lord." This powerful promise reflects the heart of the retreat—a call to leave behind spiritual bondage and follow God into a new life of faith and purpose.

This three-day retreat has been planned as a moment to welcome new souls into the body of Christ. YEF has set a clear goal to bring at least seven potential newcomers to the event, prayerfully hoping that this encounter with God's Word and community will spark something deep within each heart. Through these focused efforts, the team believes that at least two to three individuals will be led to register as members of the fellowship—taking a bold step forward in their journey of faith and discipleship.

Beyond retreat preparations, the local mission team remains active in daily evangelism. Whether through personal conversations, campus outreach, or community gatherings, YEF members are persistently sowing seeds of the Gospel. Their passion stems from a deep conviction that this season holds a special opportunity for revival—one that God is already beginning to unfold in powerful ways. In the midst of these efforts, there is a spirit of humble expectation. The fellowship is not simply working toward numbers or events, but toward changed lives. Each prayer, each invitation, and each gathering is rooted in a desire to see individuals encounter the living God and respond with wholehearted devotion.

As the retreat draws near, YEF invites the broader community to join in prayer—lifting up the mission, the attendees, and especially the newcomers who may be taking their first steps toward Christ. May this retreat be a turning point, filled with divine appointments, deeper faith, and a growing family of believers ready to live out the Great Commission.

title: YEF Arizona: A Day of Renewal and Spirit-led Evangelism Leads to 13 New Contacts
excerpt: Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) continues to carry the fire of the Gospel with passion and grace across the nation—and the Arizona mission team is no exception. On Wednesday, July 9th, pioneers…
paragraphs: Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) continues to carry the fire of the Gospel with passion and grace across the nation—and the Arizona mission team is no exception. On Wednesday, July 9th, pioneers Lucy and Hyewon experienced a day filled with divine appointments, joyful fellowship, and overflowing fruit, demonstrating once again the power of God's hand at work through faithful hearts.

Lucy and Hyewon immediately returned to the frontlines of mission, heading to Arizona State University (ASU) to continue their evangelism. Upholding YEF’s 3-3-3 evangelism standard, they poured out their hearts for over three hours on the campus. By God’s grace, they received 13 new contacts and scheduled 6 Bible studies—with 3 more to come the following day.

The grace didn’t stop there. On their way home, they shared the Gospel with their Lyft driver, who eagerly initiated the conversation and even asked for their contact information to learn more about God. These unexpected moments reminded the pioneers that the Spirit moves beyond scheduled plans and structured environments—He moves through every willing vessel.

Hyewon reflected on her outreach, sharing how she felt strengthened not by her own efforts, but by the power of the Holy Spirit. She met many Christians and even had the opportunity to share the Gospel with several Muslim students. “The strength I felt today,” she testified, “was clearly not my own. It was the fire of the Holy Spirit.”

Lucy also testified to the overwhelming grace that covered the day. “Despite the intense heat and the changes at the library,” she shared, “today was full of mercy. The opportunity to share the love of Christ again and again reminds me why we continue. Even when the campus seems empty, God hears our cries.” She recounted a powerful encounter with a student named Hallie. After a brief, missed connection in the morning, Lucy prayed for a chance to meet her again. Hours later, by nothing but divine orchestration, their paths crossed once more—and this time, they were able to connect.

These stories echo the very heart of YEF: bold evangelism rooted in love, persistent outreach powered by prayer, and a deep trust in the guiding hand of the Holy Spirit. What happened in Arizona is not merely a local effort—it is part of YEF’s greater vision to raise up Gospel-centered leaders, lay down spiritual foundations in every region, and bring even one more soul back to God.

Please continue to pray for Arizona—to be restored, renewed, and firmly rooted in Christ. Pray for the many students now engaged in Bible studies, and for the pioneers laying down seeds of revival. May their mission leave behind a spiritual legacy that endures far beyond their time on campus. All for the glory of God and the expansion of His Kingdom through YEF.

title: YEF Ethiopia Establishes New Youth Center Near Hawassa University
excerpt: By the grace of God, Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) Ethiopia has joyfully secured a youth center in the heart of Hawassa—just walking distance from Hawassa University, the leading university in…
paragraphs: By the grace of God, Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) Ethiopia has joyfully secured a youth center in the heart of Hawassa—just walking distance from Hawassa University, the leading university in the city. This remarkable achievement stands as a powerful testimony to God's faithfulness and His great plan for the nation of Ethiopia.

The journey to find the right space was filled with challenges. In a city where available and suitable properties were limited, YEF Ethiopia members faithfully searched every corner, praying and persevering through each obstacle. What seemed uncertain became possible through their persistent efforts, local fundraising, and the overwhelming support from fellowship members and the broader church community.

We give all glory to God, who opened every door and stirred the hearts of many to give generously. This mission could not have been fulfilled without the prayers, financial support, and unity of purpose shown by YEF Headquarters, missionaries, pastors, and all who believed in this vision. Their partnership and faith made this dream a reality.

With this new center, YEF Ethiopia stands at the threshold of a new chapter in its mission to reach and raise the next generation. Positioned so close to one of the most influential universities in the region, this center holds immense potential to become a place of revival, restoration, and training for countless students.

YEF Ethiopia moves forward with great hope, praying that the center will serve as a spiritual home for many and a launching point for future leaders of faith. We believe God will use this space mightily to equip young people with the truth of the Gospel and the power of a transformed life.
Please join us in giving thanks and continue to pray for the growth, impact, and spiritual revival of this new mission base. May it shine brightly for Christ in the city of Hawassa and far beyond.

title: YEF Florida Welcomes New Summer Volunteer with Heart for Mission
excerpt: As the new month of July begins, Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) Florida joyfully welcomes Jubilee, a passionate student from Riverside Campus, who has joined the summer internship program for…
paragraphs: As the new month of July begins, Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) Florida joyfully welcomes Jubilee, a passionate student from Riverside Campus, who has joined the summer internship program for mission training. With a heart full of gratitude and expectation, Jubilee shared that it is by God’s grace alone she is able to take part in this precious time of spiritual growth and service.

From her first day, Jubilee immersed herself in the mission atmosphere—visiting key areas of the YEF Florida property, joining a Bible study on a nearby university campus, and participating in a short seminar centered on the vision of mission. These opening experiences have set a strong and encouraging tone for the weeks ahead.

With a sincere heart, Jubilee expressed her deep desire to fully engage in mission life and to understand more deeply the heart of God, who longs to save even one more soul. Over the coming days, she will take part in a variety of ministry activities including campus evangelism, intercessory prayer, Bible teaching, and hands-on training designed to equip her spiritually and practically for the work of the Gospel.

In her reflection, Jubilee shared:
“Honestly, I didn’t have many plans this time, but I came here believing that God must have a greater plan. There was far more prepared than I expected, and so much to learn. When evangelizing, I hope to find prepared souls, and I also hope to learn a lot at the headquarters.”
“There is a chapel in the center of the YEF building where I can always pray and talk with God, which is such a blessing. The atmosphere is full of grace, and everyone has been so welcoming and caring that I haven’t had a single thing to worry about.”
“Even though I took a night flight and only slept two hours, I was able to forget my fatigue and joyfully handle the many new schedules. I feel a bit nervous about various things, but I’m also excited, and above all, deeply thankful. The prepared ministry, the building, the precious members who warmly welcomed me, and the opportunity to learn — all of these are truly gracious and something I’m grateful for. I want to do my best to learn everything I can here to the fullest, without missing anything.”
YEF is deeply encouraged by Jubilee's heart and prayerfully expects that this time will be one of transformation, revelation, and deeper intimacy with the Lord. Please continue to keep Jubilee in your prayers—that through every experience, she would be strengthened, trained, and used powerfully for God’s kingdom work. Let us raise more passionate leaders like Jubilee, who walk by faith and carry the Gospel boldly to the ends of the earth.

title: YEF Marches Forward in Faith, Advancing the Vision to Reach 1,000 Cities
excerpt: A shared vision burns at the heart of global mission fellowships: to plant mission centers in 1,000 cities by the year 2026. Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) is fully committed to this God-given…
paragraphs: A shared vision burns at the heart of global mission fellowships: to plant mission centers in 1,000 cities by the year 2026. Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) is fully committed to this God-given calling, standing firm on His promises and choosing the path of obedience and perseverance to the very end.

In the face of challenges—whether in evangelism, ministry work, or even daily responsibilities—it can be easy to grow weary. Yet YEF holds fast to the truth found in Galatians 6:9: “Let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.” With this unshakable faith, YEF seeks to walk as true disciples of Christ—pursuing His will through prayer, repentance, and unwavering dedication, and raising others to walk in that same truth.

At the core of this mission is the bold and joyful proclamation of the Gospel. As Romans 10:15 declares, “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!” This is the identity YEF embraces: a fellowship of Gospel messengers, joyfully bearing the truth of Christ to a world in need. This calling is not taken lightly—it is carried forward with faithfulness and deep conviction.

Just as Noah built the ark year after year in obedience and hope, YEF is called to build—not only with hands but with hearts shaped by love, endurance, and joyful expectation. This is not the work of a moment, but the fruit of steadfast faith.

YEF moves forward with clear purpose, trusting in the Lord of the harvest. With every city reached, every soul touched, and every center planted, we draw closer to fulfilling the great vision set before us. May we continue together in unity and strength, laboring with joy until the work is complete and the harvest overflows.

title: YEF Orlando Presses Forward with Campus Mission and Heartfelt Discipleship
excerpt: YEF Orlando continues to actively advance its campus mission with renewed passion and commitment. Leaders and members alike have been consistent in their outreach, both in person and online, as they…
paragraphs: YEF Orlando continues to actively advance its campus mission with renewed passion and commitment. Leaders and members alike have been consistent in their outreach, both in person and online, as they work to share the Gospel and raise up new disciples. Through recent online evangelism efforts, they’ve begun conversations with two students from the local campus—one of whom is now preparing to join regular Bible studies in the upcoming summer semester.

Alongside their outreach, YEF Orlando is also planning a meaningful fellowship event this week to connect with new students and cultivate community. The event will include a small volunteer activity where members will create handmade cards for children battling illness—a chance to extend love and hope beyond the campus.

With growing awareness of the importance of nurturing each member’s faith journey, the chapter is placing special focus on prayer and spiritual care. Leaders have recognized that this is a significant time in the lives of their members and Bible study students, and they are committed to guiding them faithfully with the help of the Holy Spirit.

To support this, the chapter has implemented a detailed spiritual log to track both new and existing students. This helps ensure that each individual’s situation is understood, and they can be shepherded with wisdom, care, and prayer. Beyond numbers or attendance, YEF Orlando is striving to provide a space where students feel safe to share their struggles and receive grace-filled guidance.

For many of these students, this is a pivotal moment in their walk of faith. YEF Orlando earnestly asks for continued prayer—especially that the leaders may be spiritually awakened and bear lasting fruit in their mission. Please lift up students Khyle, Amia, Rachel, Celeste, Peter, Hansly, and Korri, as well as others who have joined recently. May each of them experience the transforming power of God and grow deeply in their faith.

title: YEF HQ Staff Member Visits Korea for Mission Collaboration and Fellowship
excerpt: On June 18, 2025, BriDaija Jones, a staff member from YEF Headquarters, visited Korea to receive fellowship with Korean members and learn more about missions around the world from experienced pastors…
paragraphs: On June 18, 2025, BriDaija Jones, a staff member from YEF Headquarters, visited Korea to receive fellowship with Korean members and learn more about missions around the world from experienced pastors and missionaries. She shared that the experience was a real blessing, and she’s thankful for the chance to receive this blessing. BriDaija also prayed that more people would be able to come and experience the same care and restoration.
She met many leaders and members of the community. She joined the Wednesday service and had time to connect with others who are actively walking in faith.

During her stay, BriDaija also joined in mission activities with YEF Korea. She especially looked forward to opportunities to evangelize and share her faith while learning from the local team. She asked for continued prayers for her safety and for her faith to grow deeper during this time, especially through the support of the senior members and leaders around her.
She also shared some of her honest reflections about the people she’s met and what she’s been learning:

"Meeting the older members has been a unique and eye-opening experience. They’re definitely passionate and intense in their faith. I truly admire their dedication and the way they continue to fight to keep their faith strong. I can already sense that this time will be a period of real growth for me.
