I pray that I can stay humble, be open to learning, and receive wisdom and grace through this experience."
As she continues her time in Korea, YEF prays this season will help her grow spiritually, gain new insights, and build strong connections with others in the mission field.

title: YEF HQ Speaks to U.S. Mission Pioneers to Fulfill the Full Measure of Evangelism
excerpt: The General Secretary of Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF), P. Danielle White, had the privilege of recently delivering a 30-minute message to U.S. mission pioneers, focusing on the importance of…
paragraphs: The General Secretary of Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF), P. Danielle White, had the privilege of recently delivering a 30-minute message to U.S. mission pioneers, focusing on the importance of reaching the absolute standard in evangelism. Drawing from her own field experience and the advice she's received, she emphasized that the blessing and fruit of mission work only come when the full measure of effort in evangelism is given.

The focus was on the pioneers not to settle for minimal or partial efforts, but to set clear goals and press forward with consistency and perseverance. Only when the full amount of evangelism is carried out can the next stage of growth or breakthrough be expected. This means going out daily, continuing despite discouragement, and not stopping short of the goal.

The presentation tied this into three essential personal disciplines for missionaries: daily Bible study, daily evangelism, and regular weekly prayer or fellowship. These, she explained, are not optional but necessary for a stable and growing mission life. They provide spiritual fuel, direction, and accountability for those laboring in new fields.

Another key message was the need to move in step with God’s timing and leadership. The participants were urged to be careful not to act out of impatience or individual thinking. Mission work must be carried out with humility and order, anchored in faith and supported by the community of believers.

The group was reminded that there is no shortcut to spiritual fruit. The path of daily evangelism, prayer, and teaching may feel heavy at times, but it is through this full commitment that lasting results will come.

After the presentation, participants engaged in a brief Q&A. One of the first questions posed was, “If you were in our position, what would be the first thing you would do to prepare yourself?” This led to deeper discussion on practical steps and personal readiness for mission life. Then they concluded with prayer and the mission to pray diligently and to look to God always.

title: YEF Shibuya Welcomes New Brother into the Fellowship
excerpt: On June 21, Brother Oriki, a Chinese brother, signed up his membership card at the YEF Shibuya Center. He had previously attended a retreat, where he confessed his desire to live according to God's…
paragraphs: On June 21, Brother Oriki, a Chinese brother, signed up his membership card at the YEF Shibuya Center. He had previously attended a retreat, where he confessed his desire to live according to God's guidance.

Now preparing to return to China, Brother Oriki has decided to devote himself to daily Bible study for one week before his departure. He plans to go through Genesis chapters 1 to 11, and today, he listened once again to the message from Genesis chapter 1 with a reverent heart, seeking to understand God's will more deeply.
Please pray that he will stand firm in his faith and continue to study the Bible without interruption, and that he will be connected to churches in China and walk faithfully with God's Word.

title: YEF HQ Advances Preparations for Pentecost Retreat
excerpt: Staff members at Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) International Headquarters recently gathered to continue preparations for the upcoming Pentecost Retreat. During the planning meeting, key…
paragraphs: Staff members at Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) International Headquarters recently gathered to continue preparations for the upcoming Pentecost Retreat. During the planning meeting, key responsibilities were outlined and concrete steps were taken to finalize remaining details in the days ahead.

The Pentecost Retreat is a significant and sacred time for both students and leaders—a moment to come together in worship, reflection, and spiritual renewal, commemorating the outpouring of the Holy Spirit recorded in Acts 2. YEF hopes this retreat will be marked by deep grace, powerful encounters with God, and renewed strength for all who participate.
As planning continues, YEF earnestly asks for continued prayers—

For wisdom and unity in every aspect of the preparation,
 And for the hearts of attendees to be ready to receive God’s abundant grace.
May this Pentecost become a transformative milestone for many, as the Holy Spirit once again stirs a new fire in the hearts of God’s people.

title: YEF HQ Staff Member Attends GNIT 2025 Conference Bridging Faith and Technology
excerpt: On May 29, 2025, Brother Asa, a newly appointed staff member of the Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) International Headquarters, embarked on a meaningful journey to Dover to participate in the GNIT…
paragraphs: On May 29, 2025, Brother Asa, a newly appointed staff member of the Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) International Headquarters, embarked on a meaningful journey to Dover to participate in the GNIT 2025 Conference. A recent graduate, Asa has quickly stepped into an active role in mission work while also offering his skills in IT and coding to serve the global church.

Currently, Asa is working on the development of a cutting-edge application aimed at tracking and managing statistics across YEF’s international chapters. His unique role at the intersection of ministry and technology highlights a growing emphasis within the organization on utilizing digital tools to enhance the effectiveness of evangelism and discipleship.

The GNIT 2025 Conference marks a significant milestone in Asa’s journey. More than a tech gathering, it serves as a time for spiritual growth, professional development, and deeper connection to the global body of Christ. Asa shared his hopes for the experience, saying:
"Overall, I am excited to see what the tech conference has in store. I want to continue to receive grace from all of the members and share grace and knowledge with them as well."

Asa’s participation also symbolizes a new chapter in YEF’s evolving mission approach—one that embraces innovation while remaining rooted in faith. As digital culture continues to shape modern life, his efforts reflect the organization's commitment to using every available means to advance the Gospel.
Please continue to pray for Brother Asa during this important time:
That he may grow in wisdom and faith,
Be spiritually protected,
And return with fresh vision and deeper understanding of God’s love.
YEF is excited to witness how the Lord will use this experience to equip and inspire greater impact in the ministry.

title: YEF NA Unites with USA Pioneers Offering Practical Biblical Advice for Missionaries
excerpt: YEF NA met with Sister Lucy and Sister Hyewon who will be going out to pioneer in the state of Arizona early July. During this meeting time, they were given practical advice according to the word of…
paragraphs: YEF NA met with Sister Lucy and Sister Hyewon who will be going out to pioneer in the state of Arizona early July. During this meeting time, they were given practical advice according to the word of God in regards to evangelism, Bible teaching, and prayer. For the past few weeks, they had been learning seminars in regards to this so this time it was time to apply what they learned and the YEF Leader helped them to do so through her personal experience stories.

YEF NA leader encouraged them to become people who evangelize with an optimistic and prayerful and faithful mindset looking to find one more lost souls. An evangelist but be the one who looks to God people with the hope and dream that they can be saved one day sooner. It was also encouraged for them to become people of prayer who deeply care for their lambs and students with a heart of love and also seek advice from leaders as well as guidance of the Holy Spirit in how to bring the students to draw nearer to God and open their hearts to share deeply about their situations.

Later, they also shared the situation of preparing for the pioneering. The most urgent prayer topic is to settle down the housing situation as soon as possible. They are asking for the prayers in order that everything can go well in a timely matter.

Lastly, they prayed for each person's spiritual, physical, mental, and emotional health as they are preparing for the pioneering efforts. That they may prepare everything well including themselves in order that they can go and diligently evangelize without any worries. Please continue to pray for them as they come to maneuver this journey.

title: YEF Hong Kong Sees Fruitful Week of Evangelism and Sunday Service Grace
excerpt: In the past week, Pastor Andrea of YEF Hong Kong continued her faithful evangelism efforts at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), resulting in two new students beginning Bible study.
paragraphs: In the past week, Pastor Andrea of YEF Hong Kong continued her faithful evangelism efforts at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), resulting in two new students beginning Bible study.

On May 22, Pastor Andrea met with Brother William, sharing about the Christian faith and introducing the gospel. Just two days later, on May 24, she shared the Four Spiritual Laws with Brother Anzhe, who made the heartfelt decision to accept Christ as his Lord and Savior.

On May 25, YEF Hong Kong held its weekly Sunday service, where Pastor Philip preached a powerful message on John 2:13-22, titled "Cleansing the Temple." The sermon focused on the importance of spiritual purity and honoring God in our lives.

Brother William, attending Sunday service for the first time, shared:
"Today's lesson reminded me to focus on how to turn earthly treasures into heavenly treasures."
Sister Yanran, who joined the service online, reflected:
"Money has both a bright side and a dark side. We should use it to save souls and learn to find satisfaction in God, restoring and cleansing ourselves as temples of God."
The week’s events reflect God’s continued work through the ministry, as new hearts are touched, the gospel is proclaimed, and believers are encouraged to walk in holiness.
Please continue to pray for the spiritual growth of the newcomers and for God’s ongoing guidance in the evangelism efforts across Hong Kong.

title: YEF Members Participate in a Spirit-Filled Sunday Service at Hawassa Emmanuel Church
excerpt: On May 18, 2025, members of Youth Evangelical Fellowship Ethiopia attended and actively participated in the Sunday service at Hawassa Emmanuel Church. The gathering was graced by a total of four YEF…
paragraphs: On May 18, 2025, members of Youth Evangelical Fellowship Ethiopia attended and actively participated in the Sunday service at Hawassa Emmanuel Church. The gathering was graced by a total of four YEF Ethiopia members who all contributed to and received the blessings of the occasion.

Brother Selemon led the service with heartfelt prayers, setting a reverent tone and giving all the things going to happen with the faithful hand of God. Brother Samuel took time and led praise and worship, leading the congregation in uplifting songs that stirred hearts toward God.

The sermon, centered on the parable of the minas from the book of Luke 19:15-27, carried an important and transformative message. It emphasized the importance of faithful stewardship of God-given gifts, time, and opportunities. The preacher encouraged believers to invest their talents for God’s glory, contrasting the faithful servants who multiplied their minas with the one who hid his out of fear. The message also focused on the seriousness of rejecting Christ’s lordship, urging attendees to recognize Jesus not only as Savior but also as King. The congregation was called to boldly engage in God’s advancing Kingdom.

Following the sermon, members reflected on the grace they received. Brother Zecarias shared how the message awakened him to the significance of recognizing and using the gifts God has entrusted to him. He realized that the Lord would one day call him to account for these gifts and opportunities.

Sister Dagim reflected on how the sermon contrasted with the messages she often heard in her previous church, which focused on worldly concerns. She expressed gratitude for the sermon’s eternal perspective, which encouraged her to live fruitfully and purposefully with the gifts God has given her.

The service concluded with a call to faithfulness, leaving attendees inspired by the promise of joy in the Master’s presence. The gathering was an indicator of the grace of God, strengthening the faith and commitment of all who participated.

title: YEF Orlando Evangelizes at Seminole State College and Holds Grace-Filled Romans Study
excerpt: On May 22, 2025, YEF Orlando carried out a dedicated evangelism effort at Seminole State College, resulting in two new contacts—one of whom joined the group Bible study later that same day.
paragraphs: On May 22, 2025, YEF Orlando carried out a dedicated evangelism effort at Seminole State College, resulting in two new contacts—one of whom joined the group Bible study later that same day.

The study, attended by both new and returning students, focused on Romans 1, offering a time of deep reflection on the seriousness of sin, the danger of idolatry, and the justice of God’s wrath. Through the Scripture, the group was reminded of God’s righteous standards and the consequences of humanity’s rejection of Him.

One student shared a heartfelt reflection:
“His wrath is just and righteous because He deserves to be praised for creating us and the world. Since His creation has rejected Him—even after the sacrifice of His Son—it makes sense that He would be angry. God has made Himself known, so the consequences of turning away are justified.”
This powerful study left a lasting impression on the students, encouraging them to consider the weight of sin and the hope found in repentance and grace through Jesus Christ.
YEF Orlando asks for continued prayers that each student will remain centered on Christ, growing in their relationship with God and walking faithfully in His truth.
Please also keep in prayer the upcoming One-Day Retreat and Pentecost Retreat, that the students would be able to attend and receive abundant grace during these special times of spiritual renewal.

title: YEF China Holds a Graceful 10th Anniversary Service: Reflecting on the Past and Opening a New Chapter with Faith and Hope
excerpt: YEF China held a grace-filled 10th anniversary service. Pastors, elders, representatives and members, and co-workers from YEF China gathered together to witness this beautiful and meaningful moment.…
paragraphs: YEF China held a grace-filled 10th anniversary service. Pastors, elders, representatives and members, and co-workers from YEF China gathered together to witness this beautiful and meaningful moment. During the service, Pastor Yaling, representing YEF China, shared from Philippians 1:1–11 with a message titled “He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus.”

Ten years ago, the Holy Spirit began a good work by establishing YEF China. As we look back on the past decade, our hearts are filled with awe and gratitude. We thank God for His sovereign hand in guiding, protecting, and leading us. Though we’ve faced storms and trials, God’s love and grace have sustained us every step of the way. As YEF China steps into a new decade, we acknowledge our current smallness, weaknesses, and limitations, but we firmly believe that He who began a good work in us will surely bring it to completion until the day of Christ Jesus.

After the service, the pastors gave heartfelt testimonies on the growth of YEF China and offered their blessings. They encouraged YEF China to continue embracing its identity as a mission-centered para-church, to keep pioneering forward, and to open new chapters in the history of the gospel. We are especially thankful that Pastor Joel made a special effort to return and participate in this commemorative service, making it possible to hold this milestone celebration with the blessing and witness of spiritual leaders and ministry representatives.

We give all thanks to God for His love and grace toward YEF China. We pray that God will continue to lead and govern YEF China in the next ten years and that all YEF China ministers will carry even greater hope and vision as they write a new history together.

title: YEF Ethiopia Receives Grace and Encouragement from Africa Conference 2025
excerpt: The Olivet Leadership Conference Africa 2025 laid a strong foundation for African members, focusing on understanding their true identity as sons of God. The theme, “Having the Hearts of Sons, Not…
paragraphs: The Olivet Leadership Conference Africa 2025 laid a strong foundation for African members, focusing on understanding their true identity as sons of God. The theme, “Having the Hearts of Sons, Not Slaves,” emphasized the importance of knowing one’s identity before serving others. As mentioned in John 15:15, God calls His people sons and friends, and embracing this identity inspires devotion and a deeper relationship with the Lord.

The impactful session on OLI was focused on discipleship, teaching key lessons such as trusting God (Luke 9:57-62), prioritizing mission work (Matthew 4:18-22), and strong spiritual family (Acts 2:42-45). The training encouraged full commitment to God’s call (1 Kings 19:19-24), also knowing the cost of discipleship and serving both spiritual and physical families with love while bringing others to Christ.

The training was a significant chapter for the member as it created a deep connection with church members, missionaries, and pastors from across Africa and the world. The interaction with missionaries and pastors provided invaluable insights and practical experiences on how to shepherd believers effectively and nurture true disciples of Christ.

Additionally, the prayer meetings, led by pastors from Europe and various countries, were a spiritual highlight. These sessions were marked by their power and fervor, ushering in a profound renewal of the participants' current spiritual state. The unity and shared faith in these gatherings served as a catalyst for personal and communal growth, leaving a lasting impact on everyone involved.

This training has inspired the Ethiopian member to bring spiritual transformation to their fellowship by sharing the teachings they received. They aim to encourage young people to boldly embrace their identity as children of God and lead others into His kingdom, encouraging lasting change within the fellowship.

title: YEF HQ Advances Pioneering Efforts with New Ministry Materials
excerpt: As the Spring semester draws to a close across college campuses and the Summer semester looms on the horizon, Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) Headquarters is entering a vital period of preparation…
paragraphs: As the Spring semester draws to a close across college campuses and the Summer semester looms on the horizon, Youth Evangelical Fellowship (YEF) Headquarters is entering a vital period of preparation and creative development. Understanding the importance of clear and impactful communication, the team at YEF is diligently crafting a variety of materials that reflect the heart and mission of the campus ministry. Among these are specially designed cards and informational items that carry the YEF logo and articulate the core beliefs of the ministry. These resources are being carefully curated to ensure that those encountering the ministry, whether for the first time or through ongoing involvement, can gain a comprehensive and inspiring understanding of YEF's vision and values.

In addition to print materials, YEF HQ is also investing in the design and production of missionary t-shirts. These will not only provide a sense of unity and identity for missionaries but will also serve as visible symbols of the ministry’s presence and purpose on campuses and in communities around the world.

This season of preparation is seen as an opportunity for YEF to revamp and revitalize its missionary resources. The goal is to equip local, national, and international chapters with tools that are both practical and meaningful, tailored to their specific contexts and needs. By enhancing the visual and spiritual appeal of their materials, YEF hopes to strengthen the reach and impact of their pioneering work.

As these developments continue to unfold, YEF invites supporters and members of the broader faith community to join in prayer. Pray for wisdom and inspiration in the creation process, for unity among the teams working behind the scenes, and for the effectiveness of these materials as they are distributed across various mission fields. May this season bear much fruit for the glory of God and the expansion of His Kingdom.

title: Rediscovering Mission and Love: A Graceful Ending to Three Day YEF 2025 Easter Retreat
excerpt: On Easter Sunday, the final day of the YEF 2025 Easter Retreat, attendees were deeply moved by a powerful sermon delivered by Pastor Danielle White. With clarity and heartfelt conviction, Pastor…
paragraphs: On Easter Sunday, the final day of the YEF 2025 Easter Retreat, attendees were deeply moved by a powerful sermon delivered by Pastor Danielle White. With clarity and heartfelt conviction, Pastor Danielle illuminated the path of faith, drawing from Scripture to guide the congregation in rediscovering the mission that God places upon every believer.

Using the story of the disciples and their empty nets, she painted a vivid metaphor: how easy it is to lose sight of one's divine calling amidst the routine of life. But just as Jesus directed the disciples where to cast their nets and filled them to overflowing, Pastor Danielle reminded listeners that when we follow the Lord’s direction, our lives become full of purpose once again.

Central to her message was the theme of love, love for Christ, for one another, and the Church. She turned to the post-resurrection scene at the Sea of Galilee, where Jesus broke bread with His disciples. This moment, tender and intimate, exemplified the significance of table fellowship in the Christian community. Love, expressed through sharing and communion, remains a cornerstone of life in the Church.

Pastor Danielle delved into the biblical concept of love through the lens of the original Greek language. She distinguished between philea, the love of deep friendship, and agape, the highest form of unconditional love. In the exchange between Jesus and Peter, where Jesus asked three times, “Do you love me?”. Peter’s transformation was highlighted. Initially, Peter responded with philea love, but by the third time, he echoed Jesus’ agape love. It was in this moment of understanding and surrender that Jesus entrusted him with the words, “Take care of my sheep.”

This profound exchange underscored the sacred call to shepherd others, a call that is not merely about leadership but about love, sacrifice, and devotion. Pastor Danielle reminded everyone that to follow Jesus is to walk a path of both great love and great cost. As Peter’s own life would ultimately testify, ending in martyrdom for the sake of the Gospel, true discipleship demands everything, yet gives far more in return.

The Easter Sunday service came to a close with a warm benediction and heartfelt closing remarks from Pastor Danielle. A fellowship lunch, graciously provided and hosted by the local golf club, followed. Over shared meals and laughter, attendees reflected on the powerful message and their personal journeys of faith.

To finish off the retreat, the group visited New Smyrna Beach, allowing time for quiet reflection, connection, and gratitude. It was a serene conclusion to a weekend filled with spiritual renewal, deep teaching, and the rekindling of mission and love.

title: YEF HQ Enters Final Preparations for Easter Retreat with Hearts Full of Prayer
excerpt: As the long-awaited Easter Retreat approaches, YEF HQ is entering the final stages of preparation with a spirit of deep expectation and prayer. With only one day remaining before the retreat begins,…
paragraphs: As the long-awaited Easter Retreat approaches, YEF HQ is entering the final stages of preparation with a spirit of deep expectation and prayer. As many students plan to return home to celebrate Easter with their families, YEF earnestly prays that those who remain will experience an abundant outpouring of grace. The official banner and detailed schedule have been thoughtfully crafted, thanks to the generous support of a local designer and senior member in Florida. Younger members of the fellowship have also stepped forward with hearts willing to serve. They are preparing to take active roles in leading various activities, capturing meaningful moments through photography, and documenting the retreat by writing reflective articles. Their enthusiasm and dedication have brought a sense of unity and freshness to the preparations, reminding everyone of the shared joy in serving Christ together.

The love and care shown throughout this season have deeply moved the leadership. Their collective prayer is that this retreat will be filled with the undeniable presence of the Holy Spirit, and that all who participate, whether leading or attending, will receive deeper grace and draw nearer to the heart of God.

title: YEF Ethiopia Hosts Easter Retreat with Members
excerpt: On April 12, 2025, the Easter retreat held by YEF Ethiopia began with deep prayers and with uplifting worship songs led by one of the YEF members. At a later time, participants entered into the…
paragraphs: On April 12, 2025, the Easter retreat held by YEF Ethiopia began with deep prayers and with uplifting worship songs led by one of the YEF members. At a later time, participants entered into the powerful themes of John 13:1-5, guided by a sermon that revealed important insights into Jesus’ humility and love.

The sermon was led by YEF Ethiopia member Brother Selemon's explanation of Jesus’s perfect timing, as the sermon emphasized the significance of the moment "before the Feast of the Passover." Drawing parallels to the deliverance of Israel, attendees were reminded of Jesus’s ultimate role as the Passover Lamb, whose sacrifice brings redemption to humanity. Participants reflected on God’s timing in their lives and how to align with His will during trials.

In a segment focusing on the depth of Jesus’ love, the retreat explored the phrase, “He loved them to the end,” emphasizing the eternal and unchanging nature of His love. Attendees were challenged to examine their relationships and extend grace despite imperfections.

The sermon also addressed the evil doing of Judas’ betrayal, emphasizing Jesus’ response of love and forgiveness even in the face of betrayal. This causes many to reflect on their responses to those who hurt them, striving to practice Christ-like love.

Finally, the minister's call to embrace cleansing and sanctification encouraged attendees to seek God’s grace and renewal regularly. Practical lessons emphasized humility, love, and an eternal perspective, with a call to live purpose-driven lives aligned with God’s will.

Reflections from the Retreat
Brother Samuel shared, “This retreat reminded me of how intentional Jesus was with His love and actions. It challenged me to show the same intentionality in my relationships, especially in forgiving those who’ve wronged me.”

Sister Eden expressed, “The act of Jesus washing His disciples’ feet deeply touched me. It showed me how powerful humility and service can be, and I feel inspired to live out that example in my daily life.”
The retreat concluded with the members' fellowship and prayers, as participants were left empowered to reflect Christ’s love and humility in their daily lives.

title: Daily Devotional – The Power of Prayer, Praise, and Jesus’ Name
excerpt: Scripture: Acts 16:16–40 Key Verse:“Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved—you and your household.” – Acts 16:31
paragraphs: Scripture: Acts 16:16–40
Key Verse:“Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved—you and your household.” – Acts 16:31

Devotional Reflection:In Acts 16, we read one of the most vivid examples of God’s power and faithfulness in the face of adversity. Paul and Silas, devoted servants of God, were on their way to the place of prayer when they encountered a slave girl possessed by a spirit of divination. Though she proclaimed them as servants of the Most High God, her message was not the freedom God intended. Paul, moved by the Holy Spirit, commanded the spirit to come out in the name of Jesus Christ, and immediately it departed. This encounter reminds us that the authority of Jesus’ name is absolute—able to break spiritual chains and set people free from bondage.

However, their obedience to God led to human opposition. Her owners, angered at the loss of profit, dragged Paul and Silas before the rulers, where they were falsely accused, beaten, and thrown into the inner prison with their feet secured in stocks. In the face of suffering, they could have been discouraged, fearful, or defeated. Instead, they chose to pray and sing hymns to God at midnight. Their worship in adversity was not only an act of faith but a declaration that God’s power is greater than any earthly trial.

Suddenly, a great earthquake shook the prison, opening doors and loosening every chain. The jailer, assuming the prisoners had escaped, prepared to take his life. But Paul called out, stopping him, and in that moment of trembling, the jailer asked, “What must I do to be saved?” Paul and Silas’ answer was simple and profound: “Believe in the Lord Jesus.” That very night, the jailer washed their wounds, and he and his household believed, were baptized, and rejoiced in the Lord. God transformed a moment of fear and punishment into a story of salvation and joy.

The next day, Paul and Silas refused to leave quietly, asserting their rights as Roman citizens who had been beaten unlawfully. Their courage and integrity resulted in the officials’ apology. Afterward, they visited Lydia’s house, encouraging the believers, strengthening the church, and continuing God’s work of transformation.

This passage reminds us that no prison—literal or figurative—can hold God’s servants. Suffering does not prevent God from acting; in fact, it often becomes the stage for His glory to be revealed. Prayer, praise, and faith in Jesus’ authority can shake the foundations of the strongest chains, freeing hearts, transforming lives, and strengthening the church.
Application:
Consider the areas in your life where you feel confined—fear, doubt, sin, or circumstance—and bring them before God in prayer.
Choose to respond with praise, even when the situation seems impossible. Worship in adversity is an act of faith that invites God’s intervention.
Remember that God’s power works not only for your freedom but also to impact others. Your faith and obedience can lead your family, friends, or community to experience salvation.
Reflect on how you can stand courageously for truth and integrity, even when facing opposition, trusting that God honors those who trust Him.

Prayer:Heavenly Father, thank You for the power of Your name and the assurance of Your presence in every trial. Teach me to pray and praise without hesitation, even in the most difficult moments. Help me to trust Your authority and promises fully, knowing that no situation is beyond Your power. May my life be a witness to Your saving grace, bringing freedom and hope to those around me. Strengthen me to live boldly, faithfully, and humbly, trusting that You can transform any circumstance for Your glory. Amen.

title: Not by Might: The Call to Lead Through the Holy Spirit and God’s Word
excerpt: Zechariah 4:6 - "Not by might nor by power, but by my Spirit,' says the Lord Almighty."
paragraphs: Zechariah 4:6 - "Not by might nor by power, but by my Spirit,' says the Lord Almighty."

In Christian leadership, the temptation to depend on human strength is constant. Leaders may trust their education, experience, or strategies to carry out the work of ministry. But Scripture gives a clear reminder: the building of God's Kingdom is not a human achievement. As Zechariah 4:6 declares, "Not by might nor by power, but by my Spirit,' says the Lord Almighty."

Throughout history, faithful leaders have acknowledged this truth. Evangelist Charles Spurgeon once said, "Without the Spirit of God, we can do nothing. We are as ships without wind. We are useless." His words echo the biblical principle that leadership in the church must be Spirit-empowered, not self-driven.

Yet, the Holy Spirit's role in leadership is not just about receiving strength. The Bible calls Him the Spirit of Truth (John 16:13). His work is to lead believers into the truth of God's Word, illuminating Scripture and guiding the church according to Christ's will. Without the Spirit, leaders may build large ministries, yet miss the heart of the Great Commission.

Jesus Himself told His disciples to wait for the Holy Spirit before beginning their mission (Acts 1:8). It was not enough that they had walked with Him or heard His teachings; they needed the Spirit to empower their witness. This shows that the work of evangelism and discipleship is impossible without His help.

Relying on the Holy Spirit is not about seeking emotional experiences. It is about surrendering to God daily, trusting His Word, and seeking His guidance in every decision. Leaders must pray for the Spirit's help to teach, to lead, and to serve in humility. True spiritual leadership combines the authority of Scripture with the power of the Spirit, working together to fulfill the Great Commission.

Today's church faces a danger when leaders rely on business models or human logic to grow ministries. But the Lord's work must be done the Lord's way - through His Spirit and in obedience to His Word.

As leaders seek to serve faithfully, may they remember this unchanging truth: without the Holy Spirit, they can do nothing of eternal value. But when they depend fully on the Spirit and stand firmly on Scripture, the gospel can reach the ends of the earth, just as Jesus promised.

Prayer:
Lord, help us to remember that the work of Your Kingdom is not by our strength but by Your Spirit. Fill us with the Spirit of Truth, guide us in Your Word, and lead us to serve with humility and faith. May every step we take in ministry be empowered by You, not ourselves. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.
Original Devotional from World Olivet Assembly.

title: YEF Three-Day Easter Retreat: Reflecting on the Love of Christ

title: YEF Ethiopia Member Started the 40 Days Walk by Meditating the Word of God
excerpt: Here is his reflection on John 13:1 "When I meditate on 'Jesus loved his disciples to the end,' my heart is really touched because Jesus knows who betrays and denies him; however, he never hated…
paragraphs: Here is his reflection on John 13:1

"When I meditate on 'Jesus loved his disciples to the end,' my heart is really touched because Jesus knows who betrays and denies him; however, he never hated them, but to the end, he loved all. When I relate to my life, to become a true disciple of Jesus I need to follow the path of Jesus, i have to carry the cross and deny myself to do so I need to seek the power Holy Spirit through prayer so that I can live the life of Jesus by reflecting true love like Jesus did it.

We all may wonder like Peter, we even not allow Jesus to wash our feet, all humans kind have such an identity if we look at the world there are many famous and popular political leaders as well as spiritual leaders who never lay down themselves, they are not humble, that's why peter not allowed Jesus to wash his feet because Jesus is Lord and Master but Lord laid down himself and taught disciples about being servant and humble.

When I look at the life of Jesus, he was looking at nations coming through his death so that he endured a cup of suffering. Eventually, God the Father glorified him and gave him a name more than all names. So, to know the value of Joy and glorification, one should suffer, so I have to endure suffering because, basically, this world is not my permanent home. Suffering helps me to look forward to the Hope Jesus promised to us Christians. So I understood that I needed to look to Jesus, who endured such difficult suffering. Also, there is no resurrection without the cross.

Disciples call Jesus their teacher and Lord, right, but he washed their feet; of course, he is lord, but he washed their feet. It's great humility for the lord, but he did it.  So when I walk this 40-day walk, I really want to embrace the great love of Jesus. And as I am teaching the word of God, I want to be humble as well as to teach others by serving."

title: Lent 2026 Walking the Path of the Cross
excerpt: During this Lenten season, Youth Evangelical Fellowship invites members and students around the world to journey together through The Path of the Cross, a 40-day meditation centered on John 13–19.…
paragraphs: During this Lenten season, Youth Evangelical Fellowship invites members and students around the world to journey together through The Path of the Cross, a 40-day meditation centered on John 13–19. These passages guide us step by step through the final hours of Jesus’ earthly ministry—His love, His suffering, and His sacrifice.

Lent is not merely a time of outward reflection. It is a call to look deeply at the heart of Christ. As the meditation begins with John 13:1, we are reminded that “having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end.” The cross did not begin at Golgotha. It began in love. Even as betrayal, denial, and suffering approached, Jesus loved His disciples to the very end.

Throughout these forty days, we meditate on powerful contrasts: the humility of Christ washing His disciples’ feet, the dispute among the disciples about greatness, the devotion of the woman who broke the alabaster jar, and the tragedy of Judas’ betrayal. Each scene exposes both the depth of Christ’s love and the weakness of the human heart.

Lent invites us to examine ourselves. Are we loving to the end? Are we serving rather than seeking to be served? Are we responding to grace with gratitude, or are we becoming calculative and hardened? The meditations remind us that suffering in Christ is not meaningless. Scripture teaches that suffering produces endurance, character, and hope. When we understand that Christ’s suffering was love poured out completely, we begin to see that true life is found not in self-preservation, but in self-giving.

The Path of the Cross also leads us to consider rebirth. Jesus taught that those who have been washed must continue to wash their feet. In other words, we who have received grace must live in daily repentance and renewal. Lent is a time to return, to cleanse, and to be restored.

For YEF, this season is especially meaningful on our campuses and in our mission fields. As we meditate on Christ’s humility and sacrifice, we are called to reflect that same love in our communities. True leadership in the Kingdom of God is found in serving. True greatness is found in lowering ourselves. True mission flows from love that does not calculate cost.

As we walk these forty days together, may the cross pierce our pride, soften our hearts, and deepen our gratitude. May we not be indifferent observers of Christ’s suffering, but transformed disciples who respond with wholehearted devotion.
And as Easter approaches, may we experience not only the sorrow of the cross, but the joy of resurrection—living as people who have been loved to the end.
